items.t: Adapters as Data: The Latent Space of LoRAs
items.a: Moritz Grävinghoff, Konstantin Wehmeyer, Aron Asefaw, Boris A. Knyazev, Damian Borth
items.x: LoRA adapters are usually treated as finished artifacts rather than as a data modality. Prior work has shown that LoRA adapters populate a low-dimensional manifold that a linear PCA basis already organizes well enough to support different operations such as sampling, editing, and inversion. We ask what a learned, nonlinear latent adds beyond this. We train a transformer autoencoder on the same population of LoRA iden…
items.sm: Trains an autoencoder on identity LoRA adapters, finding that its latent space supports sampling and attribute editing while tolerating larger displacements than raw weights.

items.t: Computation, not weight access: large language models as auditors of clinical prediction networks
items.a: Zhiyu Liu, Xinyu Yang
items.x: Frontier large language models (LLMs) have been reported to read, edit and write the weights of small neural networks, raising the prospect of auditing clinical prediction models from their files alone. Public demonstrations, however, mixed reading raw weights with running code. We separated these conditions in internally pre-specified simulation experiments. Tanh networks of 105 to 38,401 weights were trained on sim…
items.sm: Tests whether language models can audit simulated clinical prediction networks by separating direct weight inspection from tool-assisted calculations with weights or predictions.

items.t: FedReason: Large Language Models as Weight-Space Meta-Aggregators for Heterogeneous Federated Learning
items.a: Ali Mohammadi Ruzbahani, Abbas Yazdinejad, Hadis Karimipour
items.x: Federated learning servers combine client models with a fixed aggregation rule, and each rule in common use is designed for one kind of heterogeneity. We study whether a large language model (LLM) that inspects the client models can choose the rule itself, without any training on the server. In FedReason, the LLM is called every ten rounds. It analyses the weights by running code in a restricted server-side sandbox, …
items.sm: FedReason periodically asks a language model to analyze client models through restricted code execution and write aggregation programs for heterogeneous federated learning.

items.t: FedFiOT: Fisher-Weighted Optimal Transport for Model Merging in One-Shot and Few-Round Federated Learning
items.a: Quan Minh Nguyen, Hoang M. Ngo, Bhakti Chowkwale, Yasaman Keshtkarjahromi, My T. Thai
items.x: One-shot and few-round federated learning (FL) reduce communication burden by constructing a global model within one or a few communication rounds, but often achieve lower performance than conventional multi-round FL. Without frequent synchronization, client models may drift apart, causing neurons that learn similar features to occupy different positions across clients. At the same time, local data heterogeneity can …
items.sm: Proposes using Fisher information and optimal transport to align neurons and weight parameter contributions when merging client models in federated learning with few communication rounds.

items.t: Model Merging Does Not Require Uniform LoRA Ranks
items.a: Zirong Xie, Zainab Afolabi, Nikita Kozodoi, Jack Butler
items.x: Model merging combines separately fine-tuned experts into a single model without retraining. Standard practice trains every expert at the same LoRA rank, which couples the rank choice across experts even though each domain has its own best rank. We show this coupling is a property of the merge method, not of merging. We train 36 experts on three domains (mathematics, instruction following, multilingual) at four ranks…
items.sm: Finds that merging experts with different LoRA ranks can improve accuracy for averaging and utility-based methods, while conflict-resolution methods produce inconsistent results.

items.a: Zhixu Du, Yuhan Cheng, Hai "Helen" Li, Yiran Chen
items.x: Looped transformers scale inference-time reasoning by repeatedly reusing a shared core, increasing computation without increasing parameter count. Serving prefilling and decoding with a uniform loop budget couples their costs. We present LoopDuet, a phase-dependent depth and training-free serving approach that selects the two budgets jointly while preserving decoding depth at prefilling boundaries. Our vLLM implement…
items.sm: Introduces a serving method that assigns separate loop budgets to prompt processing and token generation, improving the balance between answer quality and throughput.

items.t: Nowcasting Future Performance for Population Pruning in Survival-of-the-Fittest Training
items.a: Rico Städeli, Léo Meynent, Boris Knyazev, Damian Borth
items.x: Training high-performing neural networks often involves evaluating populations of candidate models with varying hyperparameters, architectures, or random seeds. Training every candidate to completion is computationally expensive, yet stopping seemingly weaker runs early risks discarding models that would ultimately perform better, as learning curves can cross. To address this challenge, we investigate whether interme…
items.sm: Predicts future model accuracy from intermediate checkpoints to guide early pruning of candidate training runs while reducing the risk of discarding eventual winners.

items.a: Scott Biggs, Bedionita Soro, Saumya Gupta, Bruno Andreis, Sung Ju Hwang
items.x: A challenge to Weight Space Learning as it expands from task specific and vision models to Large Language Models (LLMs) is the absence of a well curated and analyzed LLM population. To address this, we train such a model zoo for application to Weight Space Generation by systematically varying the data mixture composition between web text, books, mathematics, coding, and French across populations of 51M, 124M, and 355…
items.sm: Builds populations of language models trained on different data mixtures and uses those mixtures to condition generation of complete pretrained model weights.

items.t: Editing Large Language Models with Geometry-Aware Regularization
items.a: Bingqing Liu, Wei Liu, Jun Wang, Xiaobo Sun, Yuhua Li, Ruixuan Li
items.x: Knowledge editing has become a key technique for updating knowledge in large language models. However, existing methods neglect the geometric structure of the knowledge representation space, leading to two key limitations: they cannot distinguish which pre-trained knowledge should be preferentially preserved (core vs. non-core) nor which new edits are inherently difficult (hard vs. easy). To address this, we propose …
items.sm: Introduces geometry-aware regularization for language model editing that protects a core knowledge subspace and adjusts constraints according to each edit's difficulty.

items.t: RecSoup: Efficient Model Merging Approach for Controllable Multi-Objective Recommendation
items.a: Zidong Jia, Guofu Xie, Xiao Zhang
items.v: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
items.x: Recommender systems often need to balance multiple conflicting objectives. Controllable Multi-Objective Recommendation (CMOR) enables dynamic adjustment of objective trade-offs at inference time without retraining, adapting to shifting user or system requirements. Existing CMOR approaches typically rely on output-level reranking or parameter-generating modules, which either limit the scope of feasible trade-offs or i…
items.sm: Introduces RecSoup, a two-stage model merging approach that lets recommendation systems adjust competing objectives at inference time while addressing interference between specialized models.

items.t: Separating Common and Unique Directions for Model Merging
items.a: Shiting Wang, Yingjie Zou, Ke li
items.x: Model merging combines multiple fine-tuned models without additional training, and arithmetic methods have emerged as a simple yet effective way to merge models without data. However, existing arithmetic methods treat task vectors in parameter space and apply a single element-wise rule to directions that can differ in mergeability. In a shared directional basis, we find a consistent two-regime structure: a low-disper…
items.sm: Introduces a data-free method that separates shared and task-specific weight directions before merging models, applying arithmetic merging to shared components while retaining unique residuals.

However, such lengthy reasoning is often unnecessary for simple queries, leading to additional computation and latency. Existing approaches to adaptive reasoning typically rely on retraining the model or designing sophisticated prompting, which are either prohibitively exp…
items.sm: Proposes query-adaptive merging of selected model layers to combine long and short reasoning behaviors without retraining.

items.t: LoopKV: Loop-Aware KV Cache Compression for Serving Looped Transformers
items.a: Tianle Zhou, Yang Zhang, Tianyu Wu, Zhuohan Wang, William Nixon, Juncheng Yang
items.x: Looped transformers apply a shared block several times per token to improve accuracy without adding parameters. For models such as Ouro that keep a separate key-value (KV) cache per loop, cache memory limits the batch size that amortizes repeated weight reads. Uniform-bit quantization and fixed rules per loop do not allocate precision according to each layer's sensitivity in each loop. Measurements on Ouro show that …
items.sm: Introduces LoopKV, which profiles looped transformers to allocate cache precision and sharing by layer and loop, reducing memory reads within damage budgets.

items.t: Best-of-Depth: Learning Exploratory Dynamics in Looped Transformers
items.a: Shota Takashiro, Takeshi Kojima, Masanori Koyama, Kohei Hayashi, Yusuke Iwasawa
items.x: Looped Transformers extend inference-time computation through repeated latent-state updates, but final-depth training does not directly encourage useful intermediate alternatives. We introduce Best-of-Depth (BoD), which trains a recurrent trajectory as a candidate set by minimizing prediction loss across depths. Different valid targets can be matched at different depths without architectural changes or depth-specific…
items.sm: Trains looped transformers to produce useful candidate solutions at multiple depths, improving solution coverage on N-Queens completion and graph coloring.

items.t: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers
items.a: Minsoo Cheong, Sungjoo Yoo
items.x: Looped transformers are a parameter-efficient alternative to standard transformers for language modeling. By reapplying the same layers across multiple loop steps, recent looped language models match the performance of non-looped models several times their size. While this architecture effectively reduces parameter memory, each loop step still stores its own keys and values, so the key-value (KV) cache grows linearly…
items.sm: Proposes LoopVQ, which compresses looped transformer caches by jointly quantizing channels across loop steps and tuning codebooks to preserve model outputs.

items.t: Spectral-spatial vision test-time training for hyperspectral image classification
items.a: Xiang Zhao
items.x: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification requires the representation of contiguous spectral signatures and spatial context under limited labeled supervision. Vision test-time training (TTT) offers an alternative to fixed-weight token mixing by performing self-supervised inner-model updates on the input sequence, but its application to center-pixel HSI classification remains insufficiently characterized. We present Vi…
items.sm: ViTTT-HSI combines spectral convolution, test-time token mixing, and center-pixel and neighborhood features to classify hyperspectral images with limited labeled data.

items.t: P$^2$-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors
items.a: Sinuo Wang, Jiacheng Lu, Zeyu Zhang, Maojia Song, Rui Sun, Beidi Luan, Yutong Xie, Jing Li
items.x: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation consolidates expert capabilities by supervising student-generated trajectories, whereas task arithmetic offers a training-free alternative through linear parameter combinations. We view the linear combination of student and expert parameters as a single differentiable model and propose P$^2$-MOPD, which jointly optimizes the mixing coefficients and the student weights under the sa…
items.sm: P²-MOPD jointly adjusts parameter mixing coefficients and student weights to accelerate distillation from multiple teachers while balancing recovery across domains.

items.x: With the growing deployment of large language models (LLMs) across diverse domains, concerns regarding their safety have grown substantially. LLM unlearning has emerged as a pivotal approach to removing harmful or unlawful content while maintaining utility. Despite increasing interest, the challenges of continual unlearning, which is common in real-world scenarios, remain underexplored. Successive unlearning tasks of…

items.x: Large language models are typically adapted to a task either by placing knowledge in the input context, which keeps it external and re-encodes it on every call, or by fine-tuning, which internalizes it but demands a costly round of optimization per task. We aim to internalize the knowledge carried by a context directly into model parameters, without per-task optimization and without keeping the context in the input a…

items.t: ParaTTT: Parallelizing Test-Time Training Layers with Deep Memories
items.a: Noel Loo, Neehal Tumma, T. Konstantin Rusch, Mathias Lechner, Alexander Amini, Daniela Rus
items.x: Test-time training (TTT) layers replace the linear fast-weight memory of modern recurrent architectures with a small neural network trained online by gradient descent. This nonlinear memory is more expressive than the linear memories of Gated DeltaNet and Mamba-2, but is difficult to parallelize: existing implementations such as TTT-MLP rely on sequential, block-wise weight updates that run several times slower than …
items.sm: Introduces ParaTTT, an algorithm that parallelizes deep nonlinear test-time memories by iteratively refining estimates of their gradient updates.

items.a: Yixiao Qian, Yaxin Zhang, Song Chen, Jiaxu Liu, Shengze Cai, Chao Xu
items.x: Linear attention and state space models (SSMs) offer efficient alternatives to softmax attention by maintaining a fixed-size recurrent state, but this design requires careful management to preserve useful historical associations and limit interference. The delta rule helps reduce interference through correction of the value associated with each key, but it does not explicitly account for how related value features ar…
items.sm: Proposes Dual DeltaNet, using value-side memory reads to guide reorganization of the recurrent state maintained by linear attention.

items.a: Yue Wu, Yang Zhang, Weinan Gan, Chongming Gao, Xinsen Guo, Xiaoyuan Li, Fuli Feng

In-Place TTT recently made this idea practical for large language models by repurposing the down-projection of standard MLP blocks as fast weights. However, we find that its benefit largely disappears on rea…

items.x: Test-time updating lets a language model change persistent state after training---such as model weights, adapter parameters, or a memory module---before or while answering queries. Existing evaluations often compare systems using update count or frequency and performance measured immediately afterward. These summaries omit what is updated, where, when, and in what order. The same total can therefore hide an important…
items.sm: Introduces an evaluation framework that records updates preceding each answer and separately measures learning, retention, unrelated behavior preservation, and performance in new settings.

We investigate the extent to which these blocks can instead be reused recurrently while preserving the transferable capabilities of CLIP. We study recursive transformer backbones in which a small set of $N$ transformer blocks is applied $M$ times per forward pass. By holding $N \cdot M$ fixed…

items.t: Reactive Optimizers

items.x: We study a reactive optimizer that uses a pretrained language-model agent to inspect training dynamics and rewrite executable optimizer code during a single training run. The agent can change update rules and schedules for individual parameter groups, without optimizer-specific meta-training or memory transferred from other runs. We evaluate this approach, OPAL, on language modeling and image generation when a recipe…
items.sm: Introduces OPAL, a language model agent that rewrites optimizer code during training, matching or improving selected fixed recipes across evaluated language and image tasks.

items.x: Model merging combines task-specific expert models into a single model without joint training on their original datasets, but often incurs a performance gap relative to the individual experts. Post-merging calibration can reduce this gap through task-specific representation alignment, but the alignment objective alone does not specify which feature directions to correct. We propose Error-Subspace Calibration (ESCal),…

items.t: Agentic-TTT: Training test-time policy for test-time training
items.a: Jiahao Lu, Mohan Kankanhalli
items.x: Test-time training (TTT) adapts an LLM's parameters using signals derived from test inputs, and can make striking improvements in pre-specified settings such as IMO competitions or designated open problems. By turning deployment experience into parameter updates, TTT provides a direct mechanism for model-level self-improvement. Yet TTT is not universally beneficial: each TTT algorithm works in different settings, and…
items.sm: Agentic-TTT learns a policy that decides when to adapt model parameters, which training method to use, and when to reuse existing skills.

A continuous normalized-depth coordinate programs this mixture, defi…
items.sm: reViT repeatedly applies one Transformer block with depth-dependent expert mixtures, claiming comparable vision accuracy with about 70% fewer stored parameters.

items.x: The growing diversity of code clone types, from syntactic copies to cross-language semantic clones to AI-generated duplicates, has created a fragmentation crisis in clone detection. Deploying multiple specialized models is impractical, yet traini…
items.sm: Evaluates whether merging trained code models can combine clone-detection capabilities across domains without accessing their original training data.

Our companion study shows that post-hoc model merging can address this fragmentation, achieving 93% of multi-task performance …
items.sm: MergeSE provides command-line and web tools to check compatibility, merge code-model checkpoints, evaluate software engineering tasks, and export models without retraining.

items.x: Looped Transformers improve parameter efficiency by applying shared Transformer blocks over recurrent loops, increasing computational depth without increasing the parameter count. However, KV cache memory still scales with loop count, becoming a key memory bottleneck that limits batch size and inference throughput. KV cache quantization can alleviate this bottleneck, but existing methods often suffer substantial accu…
items.sm: ResidualQuant compresses looped Transformer caches by storing final-loop states as references and representing other loops with low-precision differences.

items.x: Geometric and Spectral Alignment (GSA) characterizes trained networks through spectral concentration, physical-channel alignment, support structure, and changes in singular bases. In this paper, we propose CHASE (Channel-Aligned Structure Exploitation) to use these structures in practical model design. CHASE covers six applications across model modification, reconfiguration, and compression. CORA, COEC, and CORAM app…
items.sm: CHASE applies geometric and spectral network structure to fine-tuning, pruning compensation, model merging, and shared attention-cache representations.

items.t: A Broader Look at Model Merging: Rethinking Implicit Regularization Induced by Task Arithmetic
items.a: Sin-Han Yang, Shih-Cheng Huang, Chieh-Yen Lin, Yun-Nung Chen, Shao-Hua Sun, Hung-yi Lee
items.x: Model merging aims to build a multi-task model cheaply by combining the weights of individual task-specific models. To perform well across multiple tasks, most existing merging methods use an additional dataset to find the coefficients for the best linear combination of task-specific weight updates. However, we identify an implicit regularization in this standard practice: searching over coefficients restricts the ca…
items.sm: Finds that directly optimizing merged model weights can outperform coefficient searches that restrict solutions to combinations of task-specific updates.

items.t: $α$Transfer: Coefficient Transfer for Efficient Model Merging
items.a: Shih-Cheng Huang, Zhi Rui Tam, Chieh-Yen Lin, Yun-Nung Chen, Hung-yi Lee, Shao-Hua Sun
items.x: Model merging offers a promising solution for combining multiple fine-tuned checkpoints into a single model through parameter arithmetic. However, finding optimal merging coefficients requires an extensive search that becomes prohibitively expensive as models scale in both size and number, due to high memory requirements and combinatorial growth in the search space. We show that, within the same model family, models …
items.sm: AlphaTransfer searches merging coefficients on smaller models and transfers them to larger models in the same family, reducing search time and memory.

items.sm: InterCorrect merges demographic-specific speech-recognition adaptations and adds corrections for intersecting demographic groups to reduce recognition errors.

items.sm: DeltaTTT trains nonlinear recurrent memory one layer at a time with local prediction targets to address difficulties in sequential test-time optimization.

items.a: Yiming Qin, Ke Wang, Amel Abdelraheem, Adam Hazimeh, Pascal Frossard

items.t: HyperNSDE: Personalized Neural SDEs for Joint Static-Longitudinal Clinical Data Generation

items.t: BACAM: Behavior-Aware Continual Agent Merging for Multi-Turn Interaction
items.a: Shuaitong Li, Baochen Xiong, Xiaoshan Yang, Xizhe Zheng, Yifan Xu, Jianhao Huang, Changsheng Xu

items.sm: BACAM sequentially merges specialized agents using interaction-based supervision and controlled updates to acquire new behaviors while preserving previously integrated capabilities.

items.t: Universal Test-Time Training
items.a: Zefan Cai, Qinzhe Hu, Ziqiao Ma, Hao Tan, Junjie Hu
items.x: Recent Test-Time Training (TTT) architectures compress context into fast weights that are updated online and queried as memory. Existing TTT designs keep this memory private to each layer: it recurs only over time, and depth merely indexes L separate memories. We argue that memory ownership need not be tied to depth, and introduce Universal Test-Time Training (uTTT), in which all layers read and write one shared memo…
items.sm: Universal Test-Time Training lets every model layer read and update one shared memory that carries information across both sequence positions and network depth.

items.t: Red-TTT: Test-Time Training for Automated Jailbreaking Large Language Models
items.a: Tongyan Hu, Hao Li, Xiaogeng Liu, Ruida Wang, Zhengyu Liu, Shuyao Xu, Ning Zhang, Ziyang Li
items.x: Large language models remain vulnerable to jailbreaks, and automated red teaming is the standard way to find jailbreaks in large language models at scale. items.t: No Task Vector Is an Island: A Comprehensive Study on the Composability of Task Vectors from On-Policy Distillation
items.a: Zhou Jingang, Feiyu Han, Han Zhu, Yuyi Zhou, Ruiyang Zhang, Jian Xu, Sirui Gao, Qingpei Guo
items.x: Task vectors provide a simple mechanism for composing learned capabilities through model merging. However, the composability of task vectors produced by on-policy distillation (OPD) remains largely unexplored. OPD trains a student using teacher feedback on student-generated trajectories, yielding parameter updates that differ from those produced by the teacher model, usually by reinforcement learning (RL). We therefo…
items.sm: Finds that merging task vectors from on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning can improve performance within tasks and when combining capabilities across tasks.

items.t: LatentHarness: Learning Latent Actions for Memory and Reasoning via Counterfactual Policy Distillation
items.a: Xiaoqiang Wang, Suyuchen Wang, Bang Liu
items.x: Long-context reasoning faces two complementary bottlenecks: retaining evidence across long inputs and sustaining computation across many reasoning steps. Existing approaches largely address them separately, with external memory extending access to distant evidence and latent reasoning compressing multi-step computation. We introduce LatentHarness, which unifies memory access and latent reasoning as sequential latent …
items.sm: LatentHarness learns when to continue internal reasoning, retrieve fast-weight memories, or emit a token using feedback from alternative action outcomes.

items.t: JEPA-TTT: Persistent Test-Time Training of Latent World Models for Planning under Dynamics Shifts
items.a: Zheyuan Zhang, Suyu Ye, Nakul Agarwal, Hossein Nourkhiz Mahjoub, Ehsan Moradi‐Pari, Daniel Khashabi, Tianmin Shu, Vaishnav Tadiparthi
items.x: World models enable agents to plan by predicting future states of the environment, but their predictions can become unreliable when test-time dynamics differ from those seen during training. We present JEPA-TTT, which adapts the latent dynamics predictor of a pretrained action-conditioned Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture world model throughout test time. Self-supervised updates accumulate across episodes, whil…
items.sm: JEPA-TTT continually adapts a world model's dynamics predictor using accumulated experience and reports improved planning across eight tested dynamics shifts.

items.t: On-the-fly Weight Generation: A Hypernetwork Proof of Concept on ARC-1D
items.a: Fabio Fehr, Philip Torr
items.x: General-purpose models can adapt to many tasks from context, while specialised models can execute individual functions with less capacity. Yet obtaining such specialists requires task-specific training or adaptation. We ask whether they can instead be generated directly from a few demonstrations. Using ARC-1D as a controlled testbed, we show that individual transformations can be represented by tiny specialist models…
items.sm: Demonstrates a hypernetwork that generates small specialist models from ARC-1D examples, with partial generalization to compositions and transformations absent from training.

items.t: Transferable Graph Metanetworks
items.a: Yuxin Ma, Adir Dayan, Yam Eitan, Haggai Maron, Soledad Villar
items.x: A weight space network (or metanetwork) takes the weights of another neural network as input and predicts properties of it. Most prior work trains such models on input networks of one or a few fixed sizes and evaluates them in-distribution. The few attempts at out-of-distribution size generalization remain limited in scope and have achieved only modest success. Consequently, the potential efficiency gains of training…
items.sm: Proposes graph metanetwork modifications intended to transfer predictions about neural network properties across networks of different widths.

items.t: PatchKV: Weight-Space Compensation of KV Cache
items.a: 이찬렬, Chanhyuk Lee, Yeonwoo Choi, Donggyun Kim, Seunghoon Hong
items.x: Long-context inference with Large Language Models (LLMs) is bottlenecked by the linearly growing memory of the key-value (KV) cache. Existing compression methods reduce the cache through token eviction or approximation, but degrade sharply at aggressive compression budgets. We propose PatchKV, a training-free framework that compensates KV cache compression methods by carrying part of the context in the model's weight…
items.sm: PatchKV compensates for compressed attention caches with context-specific weight updates computed through ridge regression, preserving the model's per-query computation cost.

items.t: ChainLoRA: Geometry-Preserving Task Vector Merging for Continual Learning in LLMs
items.a: Hang Yin, Haozhe Wang, Yuhua Luo, Zhangqi Pan, Xiaoxing Wang, Junchi Yan
items.x: Continual parameter-efficient fine-tuning for large language models (LLMs) must balance retention of previously acquired knowledge, adaptation to new tasks, and strict parameter budgets. We present \textbf{ChainLoRA}, a replay-free continual merging framework built on chain-updated task-vector geometry. From a parameter-merging perspective, we formulate a geometric view of forgetting through a measurable interaction …
items.sm: ChainLoRA combines sequential adapter training with adaptive merging to balance new-task learning, prior knowledge retention, and limited parameter storage.

items.t: Mustafa00124/knowledge-editing-dashboard
items.a: Mustafa00124
items.x: Knowledge editing experiments (FT, LoRA, ROME, MEMIT, AlphaEdit, SCR, IKE and more) with a FastAPI + React dashboard
items.sm: Provides a FastAPI and React dashboard for running knowledge editing experiments with methods including fine-tuning, LoRA, ROME, MEMIT, and AlphaEdit.

items.t: gladia-research-group/qat-transfer
items.a: gladia-research-group
items.x: Official code for "Zero-Shot Quantization via Weight-Space Arithmetic" (NeurIPS 2026). Transfer quantization robustness across tasks with quantization vectors, no receiver-side QAT.
items.sm: Transfers quantization robustness between tasks through weight-space quantization vectors without quantization-aware training on the receiving model.

items.t: Rethinking linear attention as fast weight programmers with routing and nonlinearity
items.a: Yuan Cao, Dong Wang
items.sm: Examines linear attention as a fast-weight programming mechanism incorporating routing and nonlinear computation.

items.t: Looped Transformers as Optimizers
items.a: Yulong Huang, Chen Jiang, Zhanpeng Zhou, Hongtao Zhang, Tianyu Li, Tianyu He, Xiangyu Zhang, Bojun Cheng
items.x: Looped Transformers provide a parameter-efficient approach to depth scaling by repeatedly applying shared Transformer blocks. Recent reasoning models have likewise highlighted the value of scaling test-time computation through longer computation trajectories. However, the principles for designing effective loop transitions remain poorly understood. We view the looped hidden state as a fast weight that is updated thro…
items.sm: Models transformer loop transitions as local optimization updates and uses that framework to analyze existing transitions and derive a new design.

items.t: Orthogonal Yet Coupled: Decoupling Geometric Components for Model Merging
items.a: Zijing Wang, Yongkang Liu, Mingyang Wang, Ercong Nie, Mengjie Zhao, Yunpu Ma, Kang Liu, Zihan Wang
items.x: Merging pretrained models has emerged as an effective approach for consolidating diverse capabilities into a single unified model. However, prevailing merging methods typically treat each task vector as an indivisible merging unit, overlooking the heterogeneous geometric changes encoded within it. This treatment can induce cross-component coupling: when merging decisions are derived from statistics of the complete ta…
items.sm: DiGA separates task updates into orthogonal geometric components so merging decisions can account for each component independently.

items.t: Barycentric Anchored Weight Search for Robust Model Merging
items.a: Antoni Buades, José-Luis Lisani
items.x: We propose Barycentric Anchored Search, a post-hoc weight-space procedure for improving fine-tuned vision models under distribution shift without additional gradient training or increased inference cost. Given a pre-trained initialization and two checkpoints fine-tuned on a source dataset, the method constructs barycentric candidate weights and performs a small derivative-free search along directions connecting each …
items.sm: Searches combinations of pretrained and fine-tuned vision model weights using distribution-shift validation data, seeking robustness without further gradient training or added inference cost.

items.a: @OptaAnalystUS
items.sm: Announces the NHL season opener and shares TRACR rankings, projected win-loss records, and playoff probabilities.

items.t: UnlearningSoup: Is Repeated Tuning Necessary for Large Language Model Unlearning?
items.a: Puning Yang, Qizhou Wang, Junchi Yu, Bo Han, Xiuying Chen
items.x: Large language models trained on vast corpora inherently risk memorizing harmful content that may later re-emerge in their outputs. To mitigate this issue, existing unlearning methods typically rely on training-based parameter updates, such as gradient ascent and its variants, to delete targeted content while preserving other knowledge. However, balancing the competing goals of forgetting and retention makes hyperpar…
items.sm: Investigates whether combining weights from separate unlearning runs can improve forgetting and knowledge retention while reducing repeated hyperparameter tuning.

items.t: Condition-adaptive spatiotemporal forecasting of downhole drill-string vibrations via a CNN-LSTM hypernetwork
items.a: Yuxuan Liu, Xiangyu Hou, Guang Meng, Xianbo Liu
items.sm: Proposes a CNN-LSTM hypernetwork that adapts to operating conditions to forecast downhole drill-string vibrations across space and time.

items.t: T$^2$Mem: Learning Test-Time Memory for Robotics
items.a: Yize Liu, Huang Huang, Yining Hong, Zijian Du, Zhi Cao, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu
items.x: Memory-dependent robotic manipulation requires policies to use information that is no longer available in the current observation. Retaining history alone is insufficient: memory must preserve information that supports future actions. One challenge is whether a memory-free foundation model can learn to retain and use historical information from action demonstrations alone, without external memory support. We introduc…
items.sm: Introduces a robotics framework that stores observation history in compact, updated weights so policies can use past information when choosing actions.

items.t: Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling
items.a: Oliver Sieberling, Bharat Runwal, David Jin, Ryan Chin, Rameswar Panda, Yoon Kim
items.x: Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) compress the historical context into a memory state of fixed size, thus allowing for constant-time inference. The memory state size is a crucial factor in their performance, as exemplified by the strong performance and resurgence of linear attention, which extends the vector-valued hidden states of ordinary RNNs to matrix-valued hidden states. Crucially, linear attention does so in a …
items.sm: Extends linear attention with three-dimensional memory states, using two keys and two queries to store and retrieve historical information.

items.t: Sonlowami/WS-Seg
items.a: Sonlowami
items.x: Medical Image Segmentation via Weight-space learning of INR.
items.sm: Performs medical image segmentation through learning in the weight space of implicit neural representations.

items.t: DevoteeQN/Hystar-ICLR2026
items.a: DevoteeQN
items.x: Official PyTorch implementation of "Hystar: Hypernetwork-Driven Style-Adaptive Retrieval via Dynamic SVD Modulation" (ICLR 2026).
items.sm: Implements Hystar in PyTorch for style-adaptive retrieval using hypernetworks and dynamic singular value decomposition modulation.

items.t: Controlled knowledge updating in memory-enabled AI agents: beyond model editing and recall
items.a: Gabriel Chavira, Eder Jahir Gonzalez Bravo, Guadalupe Esmeralda Rivera García, Javier A. Arcos Espinosa, Salvador W. Nava
items.sm: Argues that persistent AI agents should place new knowledge in the least invasive storage mechanism suited to its scope, durability, and evidence.

items.t: CASS: Contribution-Aware Structured Sparsity for Model Merging
items.a: Yan Li, Guiping Cao, Meng Xu, Tao Jiang, Yaguang Song, Ming Tao, Yaowei Wang, Dongmei Jiang
items.x: Model merging integrates task-specific fine-tuned models into a single multi-task model, but often suffers from parameter interference caused by conflicting task-vector updates. Existing methods typically mitigate conflicts by pruning task vectors based on weight magnitude or random heuristics, treating Transformers as unstructured ``bags of parameters'' and overlooking their inherent modularity. In this paper, we pr…
items.sm: Introduces structured masks that preserve task-relevant attention heads and neurons to reduce interference when merging specialized models.

items.t: Shallow Queries, Mature Values: Depth-Asynchronous Self-Speculation for Looped Transformers
items.a: Guanghao Li, Zihan Su, Hao Yu, Jinyang Jiang, Tao Ren, Zehao Li, Feng Lu, Ming Tang
items.x: Looped Transformers reuse a shared block across recurrent depths, making autoregressive decoding expensive because every generated token requires many sequential recurrent passes. Self-speculative decoders reduce this cost by drafting at an early depth and verifying at full depth, but typically bind draft computation to prefix representations from the same recurrent depth. We find that queries and keys approach their…
items.sm: Proposes faster decoding for looped Transformers by letting shallow draft computations retrieve fully processed values from previously verified tokens.

items.t: USA: Update-aware SAM for Cross-domain On-Policy Disitllation of Language Agents
items.a: Qiyong Zhong, Mao Zheng, Mingyang Song, Houcheng Jiang, Jiajie Su, Li Zhang, Gengsheng Li, Junfeng Fang
items.x: On-policy distillation instils multi-turn agentic reasoning through dense token-level supervision on the student's own trajectories, but a single domain saturates early, so further supervision has to be drawn from other domains. Multi-domain data mixing is the most direct way of incorporating them, at the cost of conflicts between their data distributions and of retraining the entire model whenever one domain is revi…
items.sm: Investigates why merging independently distilled language agents can hurt performance across domains, attributing failures to overlapping parameter updates.

items.t: S andhi : Fine-Grained Merging for Memory Efficient Multi-Model Serving
items.a: Vima Gupta, Oytun Kuday Duran, Nandan Suresh Meda, IkHyun An, Ganesh Ananthanarayanan, Anand Padmanabha Iyer
items.v: ACM SIGOPS Symposium on Operating Systems Principles (SOSP)
items.sm: Introduces Sandhi, a system that adaptively merges model components to reduce GPU memory use while meeting user accuracy requirements.

items.t: Using Context Is Not Enough: Test-Time Training for Personalized Reward Modeling
items.a: Bohao Wang, Xiaoyan Zhao, Yang Zhang, Jinghang Guo, Chun Chen, Can Wang, Jiawei Chen
items.x: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) aligns large language models (LLMs) with human preferences, yet most pipelines learn a single reward model that overlooks individual differences in preferences. Personalized reward models (PRMs) address this by conditioning rewards on user-specific feedback, most commonly through in-context learning (ICL), where a user's historical comparisons are supplied as contextu…
items.sm: Proposes adapting personalized reward models at inference time by encoding relationships from user preference comparisons into user-specific weights.

items.t: HyperZip: Efficient Data Compression through Personalized Diffusion LLMs with Hypernetworks
items.a: Thai Nguyen, Khang Tran, NhatHai Phan
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for lossless data compression, but existing approaches are constrained by the high computational cost and low throughput of autoregressive decoding. We propose HyperZip, an efficient and scalable LLM-based compression framework that leverages diffusion-based LLMs (dLLMs) with Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) to accelerate LLM-based data compression processes. We id…
items.sm: Introduces HyperZip, which uses hypernetworks to adapt diffusion language models to specific data, aiming to balance lossless compression efficiency and speed.

items.t: HyperIDR: a multi-scale semantic hypernetwork for identification of intrinsically disordered regions
items.a: Sicen Liu, Hanghua Su, Chen Shutao, Bin Liu
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes a semantic hypernetwork operating at multiple scales to identify intrinsically disordered regions in proteins.

items.t: GradLev: Token-Parallel Test-Time Training Via Costate Prediction
items.a: Bo Liu, Qiang Liu
items.x: Test-time training (TTT) allows a model to improve its predictions at inference time by updating weights after every observed token. However, sequential gra- dient writes make parallel training difficult. We observe that, given layer inputs and activation gradients (costates), online gradient descent admits exact parallel scans for both forward evaluation and reverse backpropagation. GradLev lever- ages this duality:…
items.sm: Introduces GradLev, which predicts activation gradients to parallelize training of models that update their weights sequentially during inference.

items.t: eval-unlearn: Benchmarking unlearning in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
items.a: Mansi, Nikhil Raghavan, Zixia Huang, Kai Sheng Ong, Ji Shen Lim, Brandon Siao Xiang Ling, Francesco Leofante
items.x: The rising number of concept unlearning techniques for text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models has produced a fragmented evaluation landscape. Methods are assessed under heterogeneous experimental conditions making principled cross-method comparison difficult. We present eval-unlearn, an open-source Python library providing a unified, reproducible benchmarking framework for concept unlearning in T2I Diffusion models. ev…
items.sm: Introduces an open-source library that standardizes comparisons of concept removal methods for text-to-image diffusion models using twelve techniques and nine metrics.

items.t: Localizing and Editing Knowledge in Large Audio-Language Models
items.a: Sung Kyun Chung, Jiaheng Dong, Qiuchi Hu, Jinuo Sun, Gongping Huang, Hong Jia, Ting Dang
items.x: Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) have shown strong performance in speech understanding, making speech a natural interface for accessing factual information.Yet they are trained on static corpora and may encode incorrect facts.Existing model editing methods localize and update facts in textonly LLMs, but do not account for continuous speech representations, or where knowledge is stored across audio encoder or LLM b…
items.sm: Introduces a speech-based benchmark and editing framework, finding factual knowledge distributed across audio encoder and language model layers.

items.t: ManiEdit: Sequential Unstructured Knowledge Editing for Language Models from a Manifold Perspective
items.a: Rui Liu, Chenheng Zhang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) inevitably generate some incorrect or outdated content, necessitating efficient and precise mechanisms for continual knowledge updates. However, existing model editing methods struggle to sequentially edit unstructured long-form knowledge, suffering from severe edit forgetting and degradation of general capabilities. To address these challenges, we reframe knowledge editing from a manifol…
items.sm: Proposes a geometric approach to sequentially editing long-form knowledge in language models while limiting forgetting and damage to other capabilities.

items.t: Plasticity Is All You Need? A Testable Proposal for Persistent Fast-Weight Adaptation in Neural Architectures
items.a: Thomas Nauheimer
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Studies persistent low-rank weight updates with protected subspaces, reporting strong fictional-fact recall at a lower learning rate after instability in the primary setting.

items.t: Ecologically-Constrained Task Arithmetic for Multi-Taxa Bioacoustic Classifiers Without Shared Data
items.a: Ragib Amin Nihal, Benjamin Yen, Runwu Shi, Takeshi Ashizawa, Kazuhiro Nakadai
items.x: Training data for bioacoustics is scattered across taxa, regions, and institutions.Centralizing it all is often infeasible.We show that independently fine-tuned BEATs encoders can be composed into a unified 661-species classifier via task vector arithmetic without sharing data.We find that bioacoustic task vectors are near-orthogonal (cosine 0.01-0.09).Their separation aligns closely with spectral distribution distan…
items.sm: Combines independently trained bioacoustic models into a 661-species classifier without sharing data, finding simple averaging benefits underrepresented taxa but disadvantages species-rich groups.

items.t: Exploring the potential and limitations of Model Merging for Multi-Domain Adaptation in ASR
items.a: Carlos Carvalho, Francisco Teixeira, Thomas Rolland, Alberto Abad
items.x: Model merging is a scalable alternative to multi-task training that combines the capabilities of multiple specialised models into a single model.This is particularly attractive for large speech foundation models, which are typically adapted through domain-specific fine-tuning, resulting in multiple customised checkpoints, for which repeating full fine-tuning when new data becomes available is computationally prohibit…
items.sm: Benchmarks eleven model merging algorithms for speech recognition across ten Portuguese domains and proposes singular-value adjustments to improve merging stability.

items.t: Accurate Source-Free Speech Classification via Meta-Learned Target-Centric Model Merging
items.a: Ka Hyun Park, Junghun Kim, U Kang
items.sm: Proposes meta-learning to combine pretrained speech classifiers for an unseen domain using limited target data without accessing source data.

items.t: Beyond the Training Horizon: Mechanisms and Limits of Length Generalization in Looped Transformers
items.a: Jia Liang, Xi Jin, Liangming Pan
items.x: Looped Transformers can generalize to reasoning chains longer than those encountered during training, but the computations enabling this behavior and limiting its extent remain unclear. We mechanistically compare two looped-Transformer configurations, which we call the Matched-Recurrence Looped Transformer (MR-Loop) and Decoupled-Recurrence Looped Transformer (DR-Loop), reflecting their respective recurrence-training…
items.sm: Investigates how two looped Transformer training configurations support reasoning beyond training lengths through different mechanisms for tracking progress and intermediate states.

items.t: JoKeks2023/tracr

items.sm: Provides a local development diary and time ledger for managing multiple coding agents, with cost estimates distinguished from actual spending.

items.t: Train Together or Merge Later? Unifying VLA Experts via a Shared Action Interface
items.a: Zhizhen Zhang, Yuxia Fu, Zi Helen Huang, Zi Helen Huang, Yadan Luo
items.x: Co-training offers a straightforward way to build a multi-task vision-language-action (VLA) policy, but can fall short of the performance achieved by training each task independently. The challenge is to retain these task-specific gains in a multi-task policy without joint post-training. Combining independently trained experts through model merging is a natural approach, yet strong individual experts do not necessari…
items.sm: Introduces PolicyWeave, which preserves a shared action interface during specialist training and uses context-guided sparse merging to combine robotic policies.

items.t: SEA-MDD: Self-adapting Mispronunciation Detection and Diagnosis Models via Test-Time Training
items.a: Minglin Wu, Helen Meng
items.sm: Introduces pronunciation assessment models that adapt to new speech through self-supervised updates to learning modules inside wav2vec 2.0.

items.t: Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning
items.a: SOUTRIK SARANGI, Yonatan Sverdlov, Adir Dayan, Haggai Maron, Nadav Dym
items.x: Learning properties of neural networks has recently attracted growing interest, with existing approaches operating either directly on network parameters or through probe-based representations of network behavior. While probing methods have shown strong empirical performance, their theoretical foundations remain limited. In this work, we study when finite probe-based representations are sufficient for learning neural …
items.sm: Establishes when finite probes suffice for learning network properties and introduces an architecture using hidden responses that outperforms alternatives on evaluated benchmarks.

items.t: VisionHOPE: Visual Backbones as Self-Modifying Learning Systems
items.a: Siran Peng, Tianshuo Zhang, Tianyu Fu, Weisong Zhao, Haoyuan Zhang, Jiankuo Zhao, Minghui Wu, Ping Jiang
items.x: Visual backbones have evolved from Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with local aggregation to Vision Transformers (ViTs) with global interactions, State-Space Models (SSMs) with input-dependent state transitions, and Test-Time Training (TTT) layers that adapt an inner learner while processing an image. Across this progression, visual computation has become increasingly adaptive to each input, yet the rules govern…
items.sm: Introduces a visual backbone with five interacting memories that jointly adapt stored information and learning behavior while processing an image.

items.t: Position Aware Layer Queries for Test Time Training in Vision Language Models
items.a: Rajat Modi, Priyank Pathak, Xin Liang, Yogesh Singh Rawat
items.x: Test-Time Training (TTT) adapts models to incoming test samples (e.g. out-of-distribution, (OOD)) when conventional fine-tuning is infeasible. Existing TTT methods for Vision-Language Models (VLMs) create supervision from several augmented views, each requiring forward (and often backward) passes through the entire VLM, incurring substantial computational cost. We observe that one forward pass with all the intermedia…
items.sm: Proposes adapting vision-language predictions with a small student model that learns from spatial representations extracted during one frozen teacher pass.

items.t: AdaLTM: Adaptive Layer-wise Task Vector Merging for Categorical Speech Emotion Recognition with ASR Knowledge Integration
items.a: Chia-Yu Lee, Huang-Cheng Chou, Tzu-Quan Lin, Yuanchao Li, Ya-Tse Wu, Shrikanth Narayanan, Chi-Chun Lee
items.x: Integrating Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) into Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) enhances modeling by providing linguistic context.However, conventional feature fusion faces performance bottlenecks, and multi-task learning often suffers from optimization conflicts.While task vectors and model merging have addressed such conflicts in NLP and CV, their potential in speech tasks remains largely unexplored.In this wo…
items.sm: Combines speech recognition and emotion recognition task vectors using learned coefficients for each layer to balance linguistic and vocal information.

items.sm: Explores sequential unstructured knowledge editing in language models from a manifold perspective.

items.t: Train4Merge: RL or SFT---Which Yields Better Teachers for OPD-Based Model Merging?
items.a: Jingyuan Huang, Zuming Huang, Yucheng Shi, Zhongzhi Li, Xiaoming Zhaı, Wei Chu, Ninghao Liu
items.x: Domain experts trained from a shared checkpoint can transfer their specialized capabilities to a single student through on-policy distillation (OPD). Existing research primarily focuses on improving this merging process, while the algorithms used to train the experts have received limited systematic comparison. We investigate which training algorithm produces teachers better suited to OPD through controlled single-te…
items.sm: Compares reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning for training distillation teachers, finding reinforcement learning teachers produce stronger students across three task categories.

items.t: MergeHEIR: Mitigating Multimodal Hallucinations as the Tax of Model Merging
items.a: Jinyu Li, Hao Fang, Zhiming Zhang, Jiawei Kong, Bin Chen, Shu-Tao Xia
items.x: Model merging consolidates task-specialized experts into a single deployable model. However, we show that such capability consolidation incurs a merging tax of increased hallucination: across 8 model-merging methods, every merged checkpoint exhibits a higher hallucination rate than the average of its constituent experts. An intuitive approach is to adapt existing hallucination-mitigation methods to the post-merge mod…
items.sm: Reports increased hallucination across eight model merging methods and proposes constrained adaptation to reduce hallucinations while preserving inherited specialist capabilities.

items.t: Routing Drift Alone Does Not Diagnose Failure in Merged MoE LLMs
items.a: Yuanyi Wang, Yanggan Gu, Su Lu, Guanghao Zhu, Pengkai Wang, Yifan Yang, Congkai Xie, Zhaoyi Yan
items.x: Model merging efficiently combines specialized large language models (LLMs) without joint retraining, but can substantially alter expert routing in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. Such \emph{routing drift} is often interpreted as routing failure, raising a fundamental question that remains unclear: \emph{does routing drift after MoE merging actually indicate routing failure, and what evidence should justify repair?}…
items.sm: Finds that routing changes after merging expert models poorly predict failures, with most expert reassignments arising from changed inputs rather than router parameters.

items.t: When the Merge Coefficient Stops Mattering: Proximity Regularized Merging for Continual LoRA Adaptation
items.a: Yixuan Liu, Yuhao Sun, Sen Song, Jin Li
items.x: Rehearsal-free continual learning with parameter-efficient adapters can be cast as a sequence of task-vector write-in operations: for each new task, a low-rank adapter is learned and merged into a running model. We propose Proximity Regularized Merging (PRM), a minimal modification to sequential LoRA merging that adds a proximal penalty during task-vector training without changing the subsequent write-in rule. PRM ac…
items.sm: Adds a proximity penalty when training sequential LoRA adapters, reporting reduced task interference and less sensitivity to the coefficient used when merging updates.

items.t: DELAYED SUPERVISION FOR TEST-TIME LANGUAGE MODELS
items.a: Jinha Kim, Taksh Kothari
items.x: Test-time language models adapt a compact memory while processing the input sequence. This perspective encompasses nonlinear fast-weight learning in LaCT, associative delta-rule updates in DeltaNet, and generalized delta-rule state updates in RWKV-7. Training these models to predict the next token does not explicitly require a fact to remain accessible after many subsequent memory updates. We study delayed supervisio…
items.sm: Trains language model memory with questions asked after unrelated events to encourage long-term retention and accurate updates to changing facts.

items.t: ProTTT: Learning to Learn Semantic User Memory with Test-Time Training
items.a: Sejun Park, Hyoungjo Bhang, Hyein Jeong, Yohan Jo
items.x: Personalization requires language models to capture user-specific knowledge from a growing user history. Existing context-based approaches incur increasing inference costs as user history accumulates and rely on separate retrieval or summarization stages, while parametric-based approaches often require reconstructing user representations when new user data is added. We introduce ProTTT, a profile-supervised meta-lear…
items.sm: Introduces a framework that uses user profiles to train an initial memory that continually adapts to growing user histories through test-time training.

items.t: New LoRA Skills Should Read but Never Write
items.a: Zeyan Li, Panqi Yang, Qirong Guo, Shengda Zhuo, Siyuan Qiu, Hu Xu, Chun Li, Jianfeng Xu
items.x: Low-rank adapters (LoRA) make it cheap to fine-tune a large language model once per task, but combining several independently trained adapters into one model remains difficult: merging the updates in weight space causes interference, retraining on all task data is expensive, and routing between separate adapters gives up the goal of a single combined model. We trace the difficulty to two choices that every compositio…
items.sm: Introduces a method for combining independently trained LoRA adapters by controlling their factorizations and directing interactions to preserve existing skills.

items.t: HyperErase: Scale-Calibrated Hypernetwork for Multi-Concept Erasure in Text-to-Image Models
items.a: Yi Sun, Xinhao Zhong, Zhiqi Zhang, Yimin Zhou, Junhao Li, Yuxia Qiao

Existing concept erasure methods predominantly follow a static weight paradigm, producing a single frozen adapter that struggles to adapt to diverse prompt variations and suffers from parameter interference wh…
items.sm: Uses a hypernetwork to generate prompt-specific LoRA updates for removing multiple unwanted concepts from text-to-image models.

items.t: ALOE: Semantically Addressed Low-Rank Operators for Knowledge Editing
items.a: Zeyan Li, Hu Xu, Jianfeng Xu
items.x: Knowledge editing changes what a model knows by modifying parameters so that a requested fact updates while unrelated behavior is preserved. This is usually treated as a write problem, but editing also involves an address problem: deciding which hidden states should receive the new residual. An update that activates too narrowly memorizes one prompt, while one that activates too broadly disrupts neighboring knowledge…
items.sm: Introduces knowledge editing operators that learn which semantically related inputs should activate a factual update while preserving unrelated knowledge.

items.t: The Tokens Remember: When Tokenization Bypasses Knowledge Editing and Unlearning
items.a: Manit Baser, Aditya Nawal, Dinil Mon Divakaran, Mohan Gurusamy
items.x: Open-weight LLMs give downstream users control over the inference stack, but this flexibility can undermine post-release guarantees that sensitive knowledge has been modified or removed. Model editing and machine unlearning are used to modify or remove targeted knowledge without retraining models from scratch. However, existing security evaluations of these techniques face two critical limitations. First, they typica…
items.sm: Shows that alternative valid tokenizations of identical text can bypass knowledge editing and unlearning safeguards in open-weight language models.

items.t: MOCHA: Multi-Objective Co-Design using Hypernetwork Architectures
items.a: Varun Madabushi, Neil C. Janwani, Maegan Tucker
items.x: In this work, we present MOCHA, the first, to our knowledge, reinforcement learning based approach to computing a family of Pareto-optimal policies across the design space of a robot using a single network. Specifically, MOCHA leverages the hypernetwork architecture to learn a network that produces specialized network parameters optimized for a given objective and parameterized robot design; we term this a multi-obje…
items.sm: Uses a hypernetwork and reinforcement learning to generate robot control policies across designs and objectives, then searches for design-policy tradeoffs.

items.t: Atelier: Learning Local Self-Supervised Features for CryoEM Volumes via Hypernetworks
items.a: Phillip Lo, Sudarshan Babu, Dari Kimanius, Aly Azeem Khan
items.x: CryoEM map interpretation requires features that are spatially localized, consistent across samples, and informative across spatial scales. Most deep learning methods for map annotation extract features from fixed voxel grids. However, implicit neural representations (INRs) are able to model volumetric data as scale-agnostic, coordinate-conditioned functions. INRs are therefore attractive for cryoEM, but fitting a se…
items.sm: Uses a self-supervised hypernetwork to generate coordinate-based representations of cryoEM maps, supporting localized features across samples and spatial scales.

items.t: Online Task Adaptation via Self-Organisation
items.a: Krsto Proroković
items.x: Neural networks are typically adapted by computing gradients and updating model parameters. We investigate whether task-specific adaptation can instead emerge from a meta-learned self-organising process that requires no gradients at adaptation time. We instantiate this idea with a Neural Cellular Automaton in which locally interacting recurrent cells maintain both a recurrent state and a fast associative memory. Duri…
items.sm: Studies task adaptation through locally interacting recurrent cells whose associative memories update from prediction errors without gradients during adaptation.

Existing approaches use inference-time intervention, model editing, or machine unlearning, but multiple plausible completions make predefined replacements restrictive. Moreover, existing studies rarely verify whether models exhibit the targeted deprecated beha…
items.sm: Builds a benchmark of deprecated API completions and evaluates unlearning methods for removing those behaviors while checking effects on other APIs.

items.t: On Emergent Capabilities and Model Merging
items.a: Luca Zhou, Emanuele Rodolà
items.x: Fine-tuned checkpoints and adapters now fill public repositories, and the most common operation applied to these artifacts is model merging: arithmetic on their weights that assembles capabilities cheaply. We ask what this operation does to emergent capabilities: behaviors an artifact carries that were never an explicit training target. Studying two independent testbeds (activation oracles and emergent-misaligned mod…
items.sm: Finds that merging can preserve shared emergent behaviors, including misalignment, but does not reproduce jointly trained auditing capabilities from separate task models.

items.t: Not All Task Vectors Need Equal Rank: Energy-Proportional Allocation for Model Merging
items.a: Hyunjoong Cho, Jinhyeok Jang
items.x: Model merging aims to combine multiple fine-tuned models derived from a common pretrained model into a single multi-task model without additional joint training. Recent spectral merging methods improve over simple weight averaging by exploiting low-rank structures of task-specific updates, but they commonly assign the same rank capacity to every task. This uniform allocation ignores that task vectors can have heterog…
items.sm: Allocates different ranks to task updates according to their singular-value energy structure when merging fine-tuned models.

items.t: Beyond Uniform Subspaces: Spectrum-Aware and Depth-Adaptive Fusion for Multi-Task Model Merging
items.a: Ruxi Gu, Zilei Wang, Wei Wang
items.x: Model merging aims to consolidate multiple task-specific models without access to extra training process. However, existing subspace-based methods largely rely on a uniform treatment of task updates, overlooking their intrinsic spectral and depth-wise heterogeneity. We identify two key deviations from this assumption: different tasks require different subspace capacity and exhibit different tolerance to spectral tran…
items.sm: Proposes data-free model merging that adjusts task capacity, spectral preservation, and depth-dependent anchoring to account for differences among task updates.

Accessing this behavioral signal requires inputs to evaluate on, which the data-free setting prohibit…

We make these relationships explicit in an operator graph, with nodes for fields, derivatives, terms, and residuals and coefficients retained as term attributes. A grap…

Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures are a remarkable demonstration of these laws, activating only a fraction of an enormous parameter bank for each token. Existing epidemic graph models and general forecasters read a short fixed window and t…

items.t: CABS+: Efficient and Scalable Model Merging via Conflict-Aware Sparsification and Adaptive Weight Allocation
items.a: Yuchen Liu, Zongzhen Yang, Binhang Qi, Hailong Sun, Xiang Gao
items.x: Model merging has recently attracted significant attention as a promising paradigm for constructing unified multi-task models without requiring additional retraining. However, parameter conflicts and knowledge interference across tasks often degrade merged-model performance. Prior work introduced Conflict-Aware and Balanced Sparsification (CABS), which reduces parameter interference through structured pruning and seq…
items.sm: CABS+ combines conflict-aware parameter sparsification with adaptive merging weights to reduce task interference and avoid costly grid searches.

items.t: StreamTTT: Reconciling Real-Time Perception and Long-Term Memory in Streaming VLMs
items.a: Joya Chen, Zeyun Zhong, Mike Zheng Shou
items.x: Humans effortlessly perceive the present while remembering the past, yet streaming VLMs often trade off real-time perception against long-term memory. Prior work shows that shortening the context can sharpen current-scene perception at the expense of long-range recall. To reconcile these abilities, we introduce StreamTTT, which writes long-range history into online-updated fast weights outside the attention context. …
items.sm: StreamTTT stores video history in online-updated weights while reserving a short attention cache for recent evidence, improving reported perception and recall scores.

items.t: The Query Knows What to Forget: A Second Erase Direction for Linear Attention
items.a: Dhruman Gupta, Aritra Das, Debayan Gupta
items.x: Linear attention keeps a state of fixed size. At long context, many stored items share this state, and interference between them degrades retrieval. Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2), like every delta-rule model before it, derives its erase vector from the key of the current token. However, the interference in its reads is measured through the query, and the erase step cannot reach it. We introduce the Query-derived Erase Dir…
items.sm: Adds a query-derived erase direction to linear attention, reducing retrieval interference and roughly doubling usable context length on one benchmark.

items.t: Machine Unlearning for Speech Question Answering in Large Audio-Language Models
items.a: Zhe Liu
items.x: Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) have recently shown strong capabilities in speech understanding and question answering (QA), but they also inherit privacy risks from large-scale training data, including the unintended memorization of sensitive information. In this work, we study machine unlearning for speech QA in LALMs, a setting that is more challenging than prior work on text-based Large Language Models (LLMs)…
items.sm: Evaluates methods for removing private knowledge from audio-language models answering spoken questions while preserving their core capabilities.

items.t: Hybrid-Policy Self-Editing for Composable Unstructured Knowledge Editing

items.x: Large language models (LLMs) achieve remarkable performance across natural language tasks, yet they are trained on static corpora and their knowledge quickly becomes outdated in a fast-changing world. This motivates knowledge editing (KE), which updates specific knowledge in an LLM without changing unrelated others. Recent works move from structured knowledge triples toward unstructured KE (UKE), where the edit is a …
items.sm: Proposes hybrid-policy self-editing to help language models use facts from knowledge updates in individual questions and multi-step reasoning.

However, their reasoning traces are often unnecessarily verbose, increasing inference costs without commensurate accuracy gains. Existing training-based approaches to reasoning comp…
items.sm: Proposes merging language models that generate detailed reasoning with models that predict directly to balance recommendation accuracy and reasoning length without additional training.

items.t: HyperFix: Combinatorial Nonlinear Correction for Task Vector Merging
items.a: Hyo Seo Kim, Ren Wang
items.x: Task vectors enable model merging without joint retraining. In practice, the subset of task vectors to be merged may vary, but many existing methods use scalar tuning for a particular subset, requiring repeated tuning across subsets and restricting task vector merging to linear rescaling. We therefore formulate merging across varying task subsets as a combinatorial correction problem and introduce HyperFix, a lightwe…
items.sm: HyperFix learns nonlinear corrections for merging different task subsets, generalizing from small training subsets to larger combinations without additional subset-specific optimization.

items.t: DiffSafeMerge: Mitigating Backdoor Inheritance in Diffusion Model Merging
items.a: Jiayang Zhang, Ji Guo, Jiachen Li, Wenshu Fan, Wenbo Jiang
items.x: Unconditional diffusion checkpoint merging assumes benign sources, yet a compromised public checkpoint can transfer a dormant backdoor while clean generation appears normal. Mitigation is difficult without knowing the compromised source, trigger, or target, and broad sanitization may degrade image quality. We introduce DiffSafeMerge (DSM), which uses a small unlabeled clean set and fixed, attack-agnostic stress probe…
items.sm: DiffSafeMerge uses clean examples and stress probes to reduce suspicious checkpoint contributions, aiming to prevent inherited diffusion backdoors while preserving image quality.

items.a: Chencheng Zhu, Xiaoyang Li, Taotao Cai
items.x: Task arithmetic composes skills by adding weight displacements, and merged models are then judged on benchmark suites. We measure when that composition is functionally additive, and find that the answer depends as much on how the model is prompted as on which tasks are merged. Across two-dimensional composition surfaces -- five model settings from 0.5B to 8B, two families, LoRA and full fine-tuning -- pairwise non-ad…
items.sm: Finds that interference between merged task vectors depends strongly on input content and prompt formatting, alongside the tasks being combined.

items.t: When Skills Meet Safety: Benchmarking and Characterizing the Adaptive Jailbreak Robustness of Skill-Merged LLMs
items.a: Yu Ma, Hongli Shi, Jing Li, Xinran Xu, Weiwei Hou
items.x: Model merging has become the default way to give an aligned language model new skills without retraining: a practitioner folds task vectors from math, code, or domain specialists into a safety-aligned base using task arithmetic, TIES, or DARE. This convenience is known to carry a safety cost, but almost all of that evidence rests on static refusal tests: fixed harmful prompts scored for compliance. We argue this is m…
items.sm: Introduces SkillSafe-Bench to assess skill-merged models, arguing that static refusal tests fail to predict robustness against adaptive jailbreak attacks.

items.sm: SharpRec addresses knowledge conflicts and performance saturation when merging language models for cross-domain sequential recommendation through sharpness awareness and salience recovery.

items.t: Modular TTT: Rethinking Test-Time Training as Composable Modules
items.a: Bohao Tang, Zhen Qin, Yuqi Pan, Zheng Li, Pengfei Liu, Ya Zhang
items.x: Test-time training (TTT) views sequence modeling as an online learning problem in which fast weights are updated by an internal learning rule. Despite the growing number of TTT variants, existing approaches typically hard-code each variant separately, which makes it difficult to design new TTT methods and to isolate the role of each component. To address this, we propose Modular TTT, a framework that represents the i…
items.sm: Modular TTT represents test-time learning as composable computation graphs, enabling systematic changes to fast-weight networks, losses, learning rates, decay, and normalization.

items.x: Open-weight large language models (LLMs) are increasingly developed through complex, multi-stage pipelines, leading to intricate lineage relationships that reflect model origin, ownership, and evolution. Understanding these relationships is important for model provenance, governance, and supply-chain integrity. In this work, we investigate the notion of LLM "biometrics" (analogous to human biometrics) to ask whether …
items.sm: Proposes identifying language model origins and shared ancestry through geometric fingerprints of weight matrices, without requiring input data.

items.t: Can Fine-Tuning Erase Edits? On the Fragile Coexistence of Knowledge Editing and Fine-tuning
items.a: Yinjie Cheng, Paul Youssef, Christin Seifert, Jörg Schlötterer, Zhixue Zhao
items.v: ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD)
items.x: Knowledge editing (KE) offers a lightweight alternative to retraining for updating large language models (LLMs). Meanwhile, fine-tuning remains the default operation for adapting LLMs to new domains and tasks. Despite their widespread adoption, these two post-training interventions have been studied in isolation, leaving open a crucial question: if we fine-tune an edited model, do the edits survive? This question is …
items.sm: Measures whether knowledge edits survive subsequent fine-tuning across 254 experimental configurations, examining implications for preserving beneficial edits and removing malicious ones.

This naturally raises the question: does such sparsity make RLVR models more amenabl…

items.sm: DOW-KE jointly optimizes weight updates across edited layers through the full model to account for interactions between layers.

items.sm: LoopMTP guides repeated transformer computations by aligning intermediate hidden states with future token embeddings and using gates to preserve useful information.

items.t: Stabilizing Extrapolation in Looped Transformers via Learned Stochastic Stopping
items.a: Hsun-Yu Kuo, El Mahdi Chayti, Patrik Reizinger, Wieland Brendel, Martin Jaggi
items.x: Looped Transformers, which repeatedly apply a shared transformer block, are an architecturally natural fit for variable-length algorithmic tasks. Although they can exhibit strong length generalization beyond the length of training sequences, this behavior is brittle, yielding high out-of-distribution (OOD) variance, even across well-performing in-distribution solutions. We trace this variance to the spurious correlat…
items.sm: Finds that randomizing training loop counts stabilizes length generalization in looped transformers, while learned stochastic stopping generally improves the balance between accuracy and stability.

items.x: For LLMs, skills are textual recipes encoding mature problem-solving experience. Despite widespread deployment, their utility is limited by the model's ability to comprehend and follow skill instructions. To address this limitation, we propose ParametricSkills, a framework that parameterizes textual skills at test time, enabling context-free management of the full skill lifecycle. Specifically, we first construct a l…
items.sm: Trains a hypernetwork to convert textual skills into LoRA adapters, allowing models to apply those skills without retaining their instructions in context.

items.t: T3R: Deeper Test-Time Adaptation for Graph Neural Networks via Gradient Rotation
items.a: Huy Truong, Alexander Lazovik, Viktoriya Degeler
items.x: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) deployed in real-world systems typically have fixed weights, often leading to degraded performance under distribution shifts. This issue can be mitigated by conventional fine-tuning, but in many real-world cases, collecting labeled data is expensive or infeasible. A potential approach is Test-Time Training (TTT), which adapts models' weights using unlabeled test data, yet it is typically …
items.sm: Uses learned gradient rotations to adapt nearly all graph neural network layers from unlabeled test data under distribution shifts.

items.t: Curvature-Guided Module Localization for Low-Rank Detoxification of Backdoored Large Language Models
items.a: Arash Raftari, Mehrdad Mahdavi, Nathan Blackthorn, Arash Mahyari
items.x: Backdoor attacks pose a serious threat to large language models (LLMs) by causing otherwise benign systems to produce attacker-specified malicious behavior when a hidden trigger is present. In this work, we study post hoc detoxification of backdoored LLMs in a practical setting where the defender has access to the poisoned model but does not wish to retrain the full network from scratch. We propose a mechanistically …
items.sm: Locates modules responsible for triggered backdoor behavior using activation patching and curvature analysis, then applies targeted low-rank weight repairs.

In this work, we present a reproducibility study of AlphaEdit, reproducing its reported results under the origin…
items.sm: Reproduces AlphaEdit’s original results, identifies a metric discrepancy, and finds that its advantages vary across newer model architectures.

However, existing methods require performing gradient-descent optimization per material for a given MLP and…

items.t: Escaping Iterative Parameter-Space Noise: Differentially Private Learning with a Hypernetwork
items.a: Naoki Nishikawa, Shokichi Takakura, S. Hasegawa
items.x: Differentially private (DP) training of neural networks is often hindered by the large amount of noise required by gradient-based methods such as DP-SGD, which repeatedly inject high-dimensional noise in parameter space throughout training. In this paper, we propose a new framework for DP learning that avoids iterative optimization in parameter space. Instead of updating the target model using privatized gradients, w…
items.sm: Generates model parameters from a private dataset embedding using a publicly trained hypernetwork, adding privacy noise once rather than repeatedly during gradient updates.

items.t: Lifelong In-Context Learning with Transformers Requires Parametric Forms of Attention
items.a: Luke McDermott, Robert W. Heath, Rahul Parhi
items.x: Lifelong continual learning remains an obstacle on the path to human-like intelligence. Modern transformers show sparks of intelligence with in-context learning. The quadratic nature of attention, however, prohibits transformers from performing this process on arbitrarily long sequences. In this work, we argue that extending in-context learning to lifelong settings is a practical solution for continual learning in AI…
items.sm: Argues that lifelong in-context learning on fixed hardware requires attention mechanisms that store relationships through parametric updates at test time.

items.t: Exposing the Illusion of Erasure in Knowledge Editing for LLMs
items.a: Advik Raj Basani, Anshuman Chhabra
items.x: Knowledge Editing (KE) has emerged as a frontier for updating specific facts in LLMs without costly retraining, but its reliability and underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this work, we examine KE from an adversarial elicitation perspective, revealing that edited knowledge is often not fully erased and continues to surface, with consistent failures observed across diverse model architectures. To explai…
items.sm: Finds that knowledge editing often suppresses original facts rather than erasing them, allowing adversarial prompts to recover supposedly replaced information.

items.t: Merging Methods for Multilingual Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models: An Empirical Odyssey
items.a: Kunil Lee, Ki-Young Shin, Jong-Hyeok Lee, Young-Joo Suh
items.x: Multilingual knowledge editing (MKE) remains challenging because language-specific edits interfere with one another, even when locate-then-edit methods succeed in monolingual settings. We study whether vector merging—combining independently computed per-language updates into a single edit—can mitigate this interference. We evaluate six merging variants with two backbone large language models, two base knowledge editi…
items.sm: Compares multilingual knowledge edit merging methods across twelve languages and finds summation with shared covariance most reliable overall.

items.t: Self-Modulating Quantum Fast-Weight Programmers for Efficient Adaptive Sequential Learning
