In this paper, we propose Self-Modulating Quantum Fast Weight Programmers, or Self-Modulating QFWP, which extends Quantum Fast Weight Programmers by introducing adaptive modulation over both newly generated fast-weight updates and historical fast-weight memory. Numerical results show that the proposed mechanism…
items.sm: Adds adaptive control over new updates and stored memory in quantum fast-weight programmers, reporting improved convergence stability and sequential prediction.

items.x: Linear mode connectivity (LMC) provides a promising foundation for understanding and merging independently trained neural networks, but existing methods typically optimize the interpolation path from only one model endpoint, limiting their scalability and effectiveness for large pretrained transformers. We propose a novel and scalable framework for enabling LMC-based model merging to {\em billion-parameter pretrained…
items.sm: Jointly learns function-preserving transformations for two pretrained transformers to reduce interpolation barriers and support merging at billion-parameter scale.

However, existing methods still suffer from performance degradation in batch knowledge editing. We identify that semantic representation entanglement, such as overlapping concepts and shared syntactic patterns, accumulates interference in the representation space and reduces editing precision. To …
items.sm: Uses orthogonal edit constraints and a gated representation head to reduce semantic interference when updating multiple facts in language models.

items.t: Targeted Recovery of Weight-Space Mechanisms From Neural Networks

items.x: Parameter decomposition (PD) decomposes neural networks into interpretable computational components that faithfully reflect the original network's operations. However, scaling PD to large models requires vast compute, making it a costly and risky endeavor. Here we propose targeted PD (tPD), which identifies only the components that process specific inputs of interest -- from isolated prompts to large subtasks -- by i…
items.sm: Recovers computational components for selected inputs, extracting a CSS submodel at reduced computational cost and modifying memorized sequences with negligible effects on other inputs.

items.x: Lifelong knowledge editing aims to efficiently and sequentially update language models over time, as new knowledge becomes available or when the model makes mistakes, while preserving acceptable performance on past knowledge. One unresolved challenge is that existing methods modify a fixed set of layers for all new knowledge samples, reducing flexibility and increasing catastrophic forgetting. Another is requiring ac…
items.sm: LOKI dynamically selects layers and constrains weight updates to preserve earlier knowledge during sequential language model editing without accessing past examples.

items.t: Quantization as a Malicious Task: Removing Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors via Task Arithmetic
items.a: Kaihsun Yang, Min-Yan Tsai, C Shijia Yu
items.x: Model quantization is widely adopted to reduce memory usage and inference cost when deploying deep neural networks on resource-constrained devices. However, recent studies have revealed a new security threat known as Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors (QCBs), where a model behaves normally in full precision but activates malicious behavior only after quantization. Existing defenses typically modify quantization proce…
items.sm: QVec treats weight differences caused by quantization as malicious task vectors to counter backdoors that activate when models are quantized.

Most existing model merging approaches follow the Task Arithmetic paradigm, which decomposes fine-tuned weights into pre-trained parameters and task vectors, and performs merging exclusively in the task-vector space. The effectiveness of this parad…

It has achieved promising generalization in multilingual reasoning tasks by aligning feature spaces of different models. However, the merged single model often fails to address the conflicts between source models, leading to suboptimal performance. In other words, the one-size-fits-all merging strateg…

Using proxy data, we find that task updates induce output shifts whose energy concentrates in a few dominant directions, while many low-energy directions can accumulate across tasks and impair performance. We call the span of the dominant directions th…

The two factors dissociate. For learning, both routes to repeated shared access -- …

items.x: Test-time training (TTT) adapts a pretrained model to each prompt via parameter updates, improving accuracy under pretraining-to-test distribution shifts. We argue that the central design question is not only how to write an edit, but also when to suppress it. We introduce RRDA, a rout…

In contrast, biological neural systems address this through fast synaptic updates that form transient associative memories during inference, a property known as Hebbian plasticity. In this paper, we conduct an empirical study of Hebbian Fast-Weight (HFW) modules integr…

We introduce two environments: MaskWorld, where agents scale weights multiplic…

items.sm: Shows that compressed transformer loops remain limited by recurrent memory size, so additional computation alone cannot provide the growing scratchpad available through generated tokens.

items.t: From Fact Overwriting to Knowledge Evolution: Causal Editing via On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.a: Shuaike Li, Kai Zhang, Xianquan Wang, Jiachen Liu, Shengpeng Mo
items.x: While Knowledge Editing (KE) enables efficient updates, its dominant Static Fact Overwriting paradigm treats LLMs as discrete databases, forcibly injecting isolated facts. Fracturing pre-trained logical topologies, this triggers Epistemic Dissonance -- a pathology where un-evolved legacy priors force the model to explicitly negate the injected update. Idealized interventions reveal that this is an inherent structural…
items.sm: Argues that isolated fact edits provoke contradictory responses and proposes causal explanations with on-policy self-distillation to integrate updates more consistently.

items.t: Extrapolative Weight Averaging Reveals Correctness-Efficiency Frontiers in Code RL

items.sm: Studies whether extrapolating between reinforcement-learning checkpoints can improve code correctness and computational efficiency without additional training.

items.t: Bilinear Coordinate Alignment for Training-Free Task-Vector Transfer

To address this inefficiency, recent work uses t…

items.t: Extra-Merge: Tracing the Rank-1 Subspace of Model Merging in Language Model Pre-Training

items.a: Zheng Wang, Kaixuan Zhang, Wanfang Chen, Jingwen Zhang, Xiaonan Lü

items.sm: Argues that tracking accumulated editing constraints can stabilize sequential knowledge updates without many specialized regularization techniques, supported by optimization analysis and experiments.

items.t: Model Merging on Loss Landscape: A Geometry Perspective
items.a: Juanwu Lu, Anand Bhaskar, Brian Axelrod, Ekaterina I. Tolstaya, T. Emrich
items.x: Model merging offers a promising avenue for knowledge integration and parallel development without retraining. items.sm: EpiMer merges models using loss curvature within a low-rank task-vector subspace and derives conditions under which this approach outperforms merging that ignores curvature.

items.t: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates
items.a: Prannay Hebbar, Yogendra Manawat, Samuel Verboomen, A. V. Ivanova, Selvam Palanimalai, Kunal Bhatia, Vignesh Baskaran

items.t: DeCO: A training-free framework for in-context knowledge editing via incremental reasoning

items.t: CounterMoral: Editing Morals in Language Models
items.a: Michael Ripa, Jim Davies
items.x: Recent advancements in language model technology have significantly enhanced the ability to edit factual information. Yet, the modification of moral judgments, a crucial aspect of aligning models with human values, has garnered less attention. In this work, we introduce CounterMoral, a benchmark dataset crafted to assess how well current model editing techniques modify moral judgments across diverse ethical framework…
items.sm: CounterMoral provides a benchmark for evaluating how model editing methods change language models' moral judgments across ethical frameworks.

items.t: Open-vocabulary keyword spotting with hyper-matched filters for small footprint devices
items.a: Yael Segal, Ann R. Bradlow, Matthew Goldrick, Joseph Keshet
items.x: Open-vocabulary keyword spotting (KWS) refers to the task of detecting words or terms within speech recordings, regardless of whether they were included in the training data. This paper introduces an open-vocabulary keyword spotting model with state-of-the-art detection accuracy for small-footprint devices. The model is composed of a speech encoder, a target keyword encoder, and a detection network. The speech encode…
items.sm: Detects arbitrary spoken keywords on small devices using a hypernetwork that converts keyword text into keyword-specific convolutional filters.

items.t: GTH-Net: A Dynamic Game-Theoretic HyperNetwork for Non-Stationary Financial Time Series Forecasting
items.a: Fujie Chen, Chen Ding
items.sm: GTH-Net combines game-theoretic estimates of buying and selling pressure with hypernetwork-based adaptation to forecast financial time series under changing market conditions.

items.t: Label-Free Cross-Task LoRA Merging with Null-Space Compression
items.a: Wonyoung Lee, Wooseong Jeong, Kuk‐Jin Yoon
items.x: Model merging combines independently fine-tuned checkpoints without joint multi-task training. In the era of foundation-model, fine-tuning with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is prevalent, making LoRA merging a promising target. Existing approaches can work in homogeneous settings where all target tasks are classification but often fail when tasks span classification and regression. Approaches using entropy-based surroga…
items.sm: Merges LoRA adapters across classification and regression tasks without labels by choosing merge weights using null-space compression in adapter matrices.

items.t: GeoSANE: Learning Geospatial Representations from Models, Not Data
items.a: Joëlle Hanna, Damian Falk, Stella X. Yu, Damian Borth
items.x: Recent advances in remote sensing have led to an increase in the number of available foundation models; each trained on different modalities, datasets, and objectives, yet capturing only part of the vast geospatial knowledge landscape. While these models show strong results within their respective domains, their capabilities remain complementary rather than unified. Therefore, instead of choosing one model over anoth…
items.sm: GeoSANE learns from existing geospatial models' weights to generate new network weights for classification, segmentation, and detection across modalities.

items.sm: Converts Stable Diffusion 1.5 embeddings and hypernetworks into formats usable with Stable Diffusion XL.

items.a: Nova Spivack
items.sm: Argues that compiling program execution into transformer weights has implications beyond demonstrations because computation happens internally and remains differentiable.

items.t: Replication Package: A Unified Model for Cross-Domain Clone Detection via Model Merging

items.t: MemDLM: Memory-Enhanced DLM Training
items.a: Zehua Pei, Hui-Ling Zhen, Weizhe Lin, Sinno Jialin Pan, Yunhe Wang, Mingxuan Yuan, Bei Yu
items.x: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) offer attractive advantages over Auto-Regressive (AR) models, such as full-attention parallel decoding and flexible generation. However, standard DLM training uses a static, single-step masked prediction objective that never exposes the model to the progressive denoising dynamics of inference, and forces all contextual information to be maintained purely through token-space attention,…
items.sm: MemDLM trains diffusion language models with simulated denoising trajectories and fast-weight memory to retain information beyond token-based attention.

items.t: Data-Free Layer-Adaptive Merging via Fisher Information for Long-to-Short Reasoning LLMs
items.a: Tian Xia
items.x: Model merging has emerged as a practical approach to combine capabilities of specialized large language models (LLMs) without additional training. In the Long-to-Short (L2S) scenario, merging a base model with a long-chain-of-thought reasoning model aims to preserve reasoning accuracy while reducing output length. Existing methods rely on Task Arithmetic and its variants, which implicitly assume that model outputs va…
items.sm: Develops data-free, layer-specific model merging guided by Fisher information to retain reasoning accuracy while shortening generated reasoning.

items.t: MoWM: Mixture of World Models via Hypernetwork-Generated VSA Transitions
items.a: Nicolas Antonio Cloutier
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: MoWM uses multiple hypernetworks to generate vector-symbolic transition functions and a learned gate to select world models for each situation.

items.t: SSAM: Singular Subspace Alignment for Merging Multimodal Large Language Models
items.a: Md Kaykobad Reza, Ameya Patil, Edward Ayrapetian, M. Salman Asif
items.x: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance by jointly processing inputs from multiple modalities, such as vision, audio, and language. However, building such models or extending them to new modalities often requires large paired datasets and substantial computational resources. Since many pretrained MLLMs (e.g., vision-language or audio-language) are publicly available, we ask whether we can …
items.sm: SSAM aligns singular subspaces to merge independently trained multimodal specialists into one model without additional training.

items.t: kaushal-09/german-knowledge-editing-gcr
items.a: kaushal-09

items.sm: Compares ROME and MEMIT knowledge editing with graph-constrained reasoning for German language models and evaluates EU AI Act compliance.

items.t: apanariello4/merge-and-rebase

items.sm: Supports model merging, task-vector rebasining, and fine-tuning for vision and language models.

items.t: The Anatomy of an Edit: Mechanism-Guided Activation Steering for Knowledge Editing
items.a: Yuan Cao, Mingyang Wang, Hinrich Schütze
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as knowledge bases, but keeping them up to date requires targeted knowledge editing (KE). However, it remains unclear how edits are implemented inside the model once applied. In this work, we take a mechanistic view of KE using neuron-level knowledge attribution (NLKA). Unlike prior work that focuses on pre-edit causal tracing and localization, we use post-edit attri…
items.sm: Analyzes how successful knowledge edits promote new facts and suppress old ones, then uses those findings to guide activation steering.

items.t: DiffGraph: An Automated Agent-driven Model Merging Framework for In-the-Wild Text-to-Image Generation
items.a: Zhuoling Li, Hossein Rahmani, Jiarui Zhang, Yu Xue, Majid Mirmehdi, Jason Kuen, Jiuxiang Gu, Jun Liu
items.x: The rapid growth of the text-to-image (T2I) community has fostered a thriving online ecosystem of expert models, which are variants of pretrained diffusion models specialized for diverse generative abilities. Yet, existing model merging methods remain limited in fully leveraging abundant online expert resources and still struggle to meet diverse in-the-wild user needs. We present DiffGraph, a novel agent-driven graph…
items.sm: DiffGraph organizes online text-to-image expert models into a graph and uses agents to select and merge experts according to user needs.

items.t: Hyper Diffusion Avatars: Dynamic Human Avatar Generation Using Network Weight Space Diffusion
items.a: Dongliang Cao, Guoxing Sun, Marc Habermann, Florian Bernard
items.x: Creating human avatars is a highly desirable yet challenging task. Recent advancements in radiance field rendering have achieved unprecedented photorealism and realtime performance for personalized dynamic human avatars. However, these approaches are typically limited to personspecific rendering models trained on multi-view video data for a single individual, limiting their ability to generalize across different iden…
items.sm: Proposes generating dynamic human avatars through diffusion over neural network weights.

items.a: namviet157
items.x: Implementation of Hypernetworks (Ha et al., 2016): A method where a small neural network generates weights for a larger main network. Features static hypernets for CNN parameter compression and dynamic HyperLSTMs for adaptive sequence modeling.
items.sm: Implements small networks that generate larger networks' weights, including static hypernetworks for CNN compression and dynamic HyperLSTMs for sequence modeling.

items.t: SCAN: Sparse Circuit Anchor Interpretable Neuron for Lifelong Knowledge Editing
items.a: Yuhuan Liu, Haitian Zhong, Xinyuan Xia, Qiang Liu, Shu Wu, Liang Wang
items.x: Large Language Models (LLMs) often suffer from catastrophic forgetting and collapse during sequential knowledge editing. This vulnerability stems from the prevailing dense editing paradigm, which treats models as black boxes and relies on coarse-grained parameter interventions that inevitably disrupt preserved knowledge. To address this, we propose SCAN (a sparse editing framework based on Sparse Circuit Anchored Neu…
items.sm: Introduces SCAN, which edits sparse knowledge circuits and reportedly preserves language model capabilities through 3,000 sequential knowledge updates.

items.t: Beyond the Covariance Trap: Unlocking Generalization in Same-Subject Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models
items.a: Xiyu Liu, Qingyi Si, Zhengxiao Liu, Chenxu Yang, Naibin Gu, Zheng Lin
items.x: While locate-then-edit knowledge editing efficiently updates knowledge encoded within Large Language Models (LLMs), a critical generalization failure mode emerges in the practical same-subject knowledge editing scenario: models fail to recall the updated knowledge when following user instructions, despite successfully recalling it in the original edited form. This paper identifies the geometric root of this generaliz…
items.sm: Attributes failures to recall edited knowledge under varied prompts to unstable optimization and covariance constraints that amplify changes in internal activations.

While model merging is an efficient method to combine the different modalities into a unified MLLM, existing methods rely on input-agnostic parameter space heur…

items.t: On the Superimposed Noise Accumulation Problem in Sequential Knowledge Editing of Large Language Models
items.a: Ding Cao, Yuchen Cai, Yuqing Huang, Xuesong He, Rongxi Guo, Guiquan Liu, Guangzhong Sun
items.v: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
items.x: Sequential knowledge editing techniques aim to continuously update knowledge in large language models at low cost, preventing models from generating outdated or incorrect information. However, existing sequential editing methods suffer from a significant decline in editing success rates after long-term editing. Through theoretical analysis and experiments, our findings reveal that as the number of edits increases, th…

This potential has been partly driven by the success of general-purpose vision models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM), which has inspired the development of various fine-tuned variants for medical segment…

Model merging offers a compelling alternative by directly integrating the weights of multiple source models without requiring additional data or extensive training. However, conventional model merging techniques, such as parameter averaging, often suffer from the unintended combination of non-ge…
items.sm: Proposes M-Loss to measure model merging compatibility using limited unlabeled data.

items.t: Uncovering and Mitigating Transient Blindness in Multimodal Model Editing

items.x: Multimodal Model Editing (MMED) aims to correct erroneous knowledge in multimodal models. Existing evaluation methods, adapted from textual model editing, overstate success by relying on low-similarity or random inputs, obscure overfitting. We propose a comprehensive locality evaluation framework, covering three key dimensions: random-image locality, no-image locality, and consistent-image locality, operationalized t…
items.sm: Finds that multimodal knowledge edits can cause models to ignore images and proposes broader evaluations and adversarial losses to address this behavior.

items.t: Model Editing as a Double-Edged Sword: Steering Agent Behavior Toward Beneficence or Harm
items.a: Baixiang Huang, Zhen Tan, Haoran Wang, Zijie Liu, Dawei Li, Ali Payani, Huan Liu, Tianlong Chen

items.t: Editing as Unlearning: Are Knowledge Editing Methods Strong Baselines for Large Language Model Unlearning?
items.a: Zexi Li, xianghui wang, William F. Shen, Meghdad Kurmanji, Xinchi Qiu, Dongqi Cai, Cheng Wu, Nicholas D. Lane
items.v: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
items.x: Large language Model (LLM) unlearning, i.e., selectively removing information from LLMs, is vital for responsible model deployment. Differently, LLM knowledge editing aims to modify LLM knowledge instead of removing it. Though editing and unlearning seem to be two distinct tasks, we find there is a tight connection between them. In this paper, we conceptualize unlearning as a special case of editing where information…
items.sm: Evaluates knowledge editing as an unlearning strategy and finds WISE and AlphaEdit effective at replacing targeted information with refusal or empty responses.

items.t: MedMKEB: A Comprehensive Knowledge Editing Benchmark for Medical Multimodal Large Language Models

items.x: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have significantly improved medical AI, enabling it to unify the understanding of visual and textual information. However, as medical knowledge continues to evolve, it is critical to allow these models to efficiently update outdated or incorrect information without retraining from scratch. Although textual knowledge editing has been widely studied, there is …
items.sm: Introduces MedMKEB, a benchmark assessing the reliability, generality, locality, portability, and robustness of knowledge edits in medical models processing images and text.

items.t: MultiMedBench: A Scenario-Aware Benchmark for Evaluating Knowledge Editing in Medical VQA

items.t: CP-CLIP: Customized Parameter Generation for Open-vocabulary Semantic Segmentation

items.t: Multiplicative Orthogonal Sequential Editing for Language Models

items.t: Can Editing LLMs Inject Harm?

items.x: Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as a new information channel. In this paper, we propose to reformulate knowledge editing as a new type of safety threat for LLMs, namely Editing Attack, and conduct a systematic investigation with a newly constructed datase…

The first paradigm designs multi-domain or multi-task instruction data for generalizable recommendation, so as to align LLMs with genera…
items.sm: Introduces RecCocktail, a recommendation framework combining general recommendation training with domain specialization to support both new and established recommendation settings.

items.t: MetaKE: Meta-Learning for Knowledge Editing Toward a Better Accuracy-Editability Trade-off
items.a: Shuxin Liu, Di Gao, Ou Wu
items.x: Existing locate-then-edit Knowledge Editing (KE) methods typically decompose editing into two stages: upstream target representation optimization and downstream constrained parameter optimization. The optimization across the two stages is disconnected: upstream applies uniform regularization without observing downstream realization of the planned residual, hindering a refined accuracy-editability trade-off. Since thi…

items.x: Model merging has shown that multitask models can be created by directly combining the parameters of different models that are each specialized on tasks of interest. However, models trained independently on distinct tasks often exhibit interference that degrades the merged model's performance. To solve this problem, we formally define the notion of Cross-Task Interference as the drift in the representation of the mer…
items.sm: Proposes adapting task experts with unlabeled auxiliary data to reduce interference when their parameters are merged into a multitask model.

items.x: The dynamic evolution of real-world necessitates model editing within Large Language Models. While existing methods explore modular isolation or parameter-efficient strategies, they still suffer from semantic drift or knowledge forgetting due to continual updating. To address these challenges, we propose SoLA, a Semantic routing-based LoRA framework for lifelong model editing. In SoLA, each edit is encapsulated as an…
items.sm: Introduces SoLA, which stores edits in separate frozen LoRA modules, routes inputs semantically, and allows individual edits to be revoked.

items.t: Sparse Task Vector Mixup with Hypernetworks for Efficient Knowledge Transfer in Whole-Slide Image Prognosis

However, the available training samples for one cancer type are usually scarce in pathology. Consequently, the model often struggles to learn generalizable knowledge, thus performing worse on the tumor samples with inherent high heterogeneity. Although multi-…
items.sm: Proposes STEPH, which uses sparse task vector mixing and hypernetworks to transfer knowledge between cancer models for prognosis from whole-slide images.

items.t: Model Merging in the Era of Large Language Models: Methods, Applications, and Future Directions
items.a: Mingyang Song, Mao Zheng
items.x: Model merging combines the parameters of multiple neural networks into a single model without additional training. As fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) proliferate, merging offers a computationally efficient alternative to ensembles and full retraining, enabling practitioners to compose specialized capabilities at minimal cost. This survey examines model merging in the LLM era through the \textbf{FUSE} taxonomy…
items.sm: Surveys language model merging through a taxonomy covering theoretical foundations, combination strategies, application scenarios, and the surrounding ecosystem.

items.a: Xiaolong Han, Zehong Wang, Bo Zhao, Binchi Zhang, Jundong Li, Damian Borth, Rose Yu, Haggai Maron
items.x: Neural network weights are typically viewed as the end product of training, while most deep learning research focuses on data, features, and architectures. However, recent advances show that the set of all possible weight values (weight space) itself contains rich structure: pretrained models form organized distributions, exhibit symmetries, and can be embedded, compared, or even generated. Understanding such structu…
items.sm: Surveys methods for understanding, representing, and generating neural network weights, treating weight space as a structured domain for analysis and modeling.

items.t: An Empirical Study and Theoretical Explanation on Task-Level Model-Merging Collapse
items.a: Yuan Cao, Dezhi Ran, Y. Guo, M.S. Wu, Simin Chen, Linyi Li, Wei Yang, Tao Xie
items.x: Model merging unifies independently fine-tuned LLMs from the same base, enabling reuse and integration of parallel development efforts without retraining. However, in practice we observe that merging does not always succeed: certain combinations of task-specialist models suffer from catastrophic performance degradation after merging. We refer to this failure mode as merging collapse. Intuitively, collapse arises when…
items.sm: Investigates severe performance failures when merging certain task specialists and examines representational incompatibility as an explanation for collapse across merging methods.

Training on each dataset produces a new set of model weights, resulting in a multitude of checkpoints saved in-house or on open-source platforms. However, these training artifacts are rarely reused for subsequent experiments despite containing improved model abilities for potentially similar tasks. In th…

NFAS departs from conventional alignment approaches that rely on layer-wise features or task-specific activations by modeling the intrinsic dynamical evolution of stimulus representations across network depth. Specifically, we model layer-wis…
items.sm: Introduces a brain-referenced framework for comparing neural networks by extracting stable patterns across network depth and mapping them onto coordinates defined by neural responses.

In this work, we introduce Neural Network Diffusion Transformers (NNiTs), whi…

Current existing learnin…
items.sm: HyperKKL uses a hypernetwork conditioned on external inputs to generate observer parameters for estimating states in driven nonlinear systems.

items.t: VGG-T$^3$: Offline Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction at Scale

Our approach is built on the key insight that this bottleneck stems from the varying-length Key-Value (KV) space representation of scene geometry, which we distill into a fixed-size Multi-Layer Perceptron (…
items.sm: VGG-T³ compresses scene information into fixed-size neural network weights through test-time training, enabling 3D reconstruction with computation growing linearly with image count.

items.t: SR-TTT Does Not Learn Retrieval: A Correction and Mechanistic Post-Mortem of Surprisal-Aware Residual Test-Time Training
items.a: Swamynathan V P
items.x: Test-Time Training (TTT) language models replace the KV-cache with fast weights updated during inference, achieving O(1) memory but suffering catastrophic failure on exact-recall tasks. Version 1 of this work proposed SR-TTT, which routes high-surprisal tokens to a sparse exact-attention Residual Cache, and reported large Needle-in-a-Haystack gains. We show those gains were evaluation artifacts: the loss and metric r…
items.sm: Corrects evaluation and causality errors behind previously reported SR-TTT retrieval gains and finds that the proposed retrieval mechanism fails under corrected testing.

items.t: Hypernetwork-based approach for grid-independent functional data clustering
items.a: Anirudh Thatipelli, Ali Siahkoohi
items.x: Functional data clustering is concerned with grouping functions that share similar structure, yet most existing methods implicitly operate on sampled grids, causing cluster assignments to depend on resolution, sampling density, or preprocessing choices rather than on the underlying functions themselves. To address this limitation, we introduce a framework that maps discretized function observations -- at arbitrary re…
items.sm: Uses a hypernetwork autoencoder to represent sampled functions compactly, allowing clustering that is independent of sampling grids and resolution.

items.t: Per-FedDMA: A personalized federated learning method based on deep multisampling and hypernetwork dynamic adaptation
items.a: Wei Liu, Ying Wang, Bin Wang, Guangjun Zai, Wei She, Tian Qi Zhao

items.t: Meta-Reinforcement Learning with Hypernetworks for Variable Speed Limit Control under Adverse Weather and Work Zones

items.t: RAIN-Merging: A Gradient-Free Method to Enhance Instruction Following in Large Reasoning Models with Preserved Thinking Format
items.a: Zhehao Huang, Yuhang Liu, Baijiong Lin, Yixin Lou, Zhengbao He, Hanling Tian, Tao Li, Xiaolin Huang
items.x: Large reasoning models (LRMs) excel at a long chain of reasoning but often fail to faithfully follow instructions regarding output format, constraints, or specific requirements. We investigate whether this gap can be closed by integrating an instruction-tuned model (ITM) into an LRM. Analyzing their differences in parameter space, namely task vectors, we find that their principal subspaces are nearly orthogonal acros…
items.sm: RAIN-Merging combines instruction-tuned and reasoning models without gradient updates to improve instruction following while preserving reasoning ability and thinking format.

items.t: The Mean is the Mirage: Entropy-Adaptive Model Merging under Heterogeneous Domain Shifts in Medical Imaging
items.a: Sameer Ambekar, Reza Nasirigerdeh, Peter J. Schüffler, Lina Felsner, Daniel M. Lang, Julia A. Schnabel
items.x: Model merging under unseen test-time distribution shifts often renders naive strategies, such as mean averaging unreliable. This challenge is especially acute in medical imaging, where models are fine-tuned locally at clinics on private data, producing domain-specific models that differ by scanner, protocol, and population. When deployed at an unseen clinical site, test cases arrive in unlabeled, non-i.i.d. batches, …
items.sm: Adapts medical imaging models to unlabeled incoming batches using entropy-guided model merging, with separate merging of encoders and classification heads.

items.t: Transcoder Adapters for Reasoning-Model Diffing
items.a: Nathan Hu, Jake Ward, Thomas Icard, Christopher Potts
items.x: While reasoning models are increasingly ubiquitous, the effects of reasoning training on a model's internal mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this work, we introduce transcoder adapters, a technique for learning an interpretable approximation of the difference in MLP computation before and after fine-tuning. We apply transcoder adapters to characterize the differences between Qwen2.5-Math-7B and its reasoning-d…
items.sm: Introduces interpretable transcoder adapters that approximate computational changes from reasoning fine-tuning and recover much of the resulting reasoning accuracy improvement.

items.t: Test-Time Training with KV Binding Is Secretly Linear Attention
items.a: Junchen Liu, Sven Elflein, Or Litany, Žan Gojčič, Ruilong Li
items.x: Test-time training (TTT) with KV binding as sequence modeling layer is commonly interpreted as a form of online meta-learning that memorizes a key-value mapping at test time. However, our analysis reveals multiple phenomena that contradict this memorization-based interpretation. Motivated by these findings, we revisit the formulation of TTT and show that a broad class of TTT architectures can be expressed as a form o…
items.sm: Shows that a broad class of test-time training architectures with key-value binding can be expressed as learned linear attention, enabling simplification and parallel computation.

items.t: Learning from Trials and Errors: Reflective Test-Time Planning for Embodied LLMs
items.a: Yining Hong, Huang Huang, Manling Li, Li Fei-Fei, Leonidas Guibas, Jiajun Wu, Yejin Choi
items.x: Embodied LLMs endow robots with high-level task reasoning, but they cannot reflect on what went wrong or why, turning deployment into a sequence of independent trials where mistakes repeat rather than accumulate into experience. Drawing upon human reflective practitioners, we introduce Reflective Test-Time Planning, which integrates two modes of reflection: \textit{reflection-in-action}, where the agent uses test-tim…
items.sm: Enables embodied language models to compare actions before execution and update their reflection and action models using feedback and retrospective evaluation.

items.sm: Provides code for DC-Merge, a method intended to improve model merging through directional consistency.

items.t: Model Merging in the Essential Subspace
items.a: Longhua Li, Lei Qi, Qi Tian, Xin Geng
items.x: Model merging aims to integrate multiple task-specific fine-tuned models derived from a shared pre-trained checkpoint into a single multi-task model without additional training. Despite extensive research, task interference remains a major obstacle that often undermines the performance of merged models. In this paper, we propose ESM (Essential Subspace Merging) , a robust framework for effective model merging. We beg…
items.sm: Reduces interference during model merging by projecting task-specific parameter updates onto principal subspaces identified from changes in feature representations.

items.t: Training-Free Merging of Heterogeneous Models via Activation-Driven Neuron Matching
items.a: Shuo An, Ke Qin, Dongyang Zhang, Xin Wu
items.sm: A-EMM uses neuron activations to guide training-free merging of models with different initializations and heterogeneous structures.

items.t: tttLRM: Test-Time Training for Long Context and Autoregressive 3D Reconstruction
items.a: Chen Wang, Hao Tan, Yifan Wang, Zhiqin Chen, Yuheng Liu, Kalyan Sunkavalli, Sai Bi, Lingjie Liu
items.x: We propose tttLRM, a novel large 3D reconstruction model that leverages a Test-Time Training (TTT) layer to enable long-context, autoregressive 3D reconstruction with linear computational complexity, further scaling the model's capability. items.sm: tttLRM compresses image observations into fast weights for long-context, autoregressive 3D reconstruction with linear computational complexity and progressive refinement from streaming images.

items.t: Comparison of Weight-Space LLM Merging Methods
items.a: Furel TEGUIMENE YENDJI, Azanzi Jiomekong, Sanju Mishra Tiwari
items.sm: Compares methods for merging large language models in weight space.

items.t: Golden Layers and Where to Find Them: Improved Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models Via Layer Gradient Analysis
items.a: Shrestha Datta, Hongfu Liu, Anshuman Chhabra
items.x: Knowledge editing in Large Language Models (LLMs) aims to update the model's prediction for a specific query to a desired target while preserving its behavior on all other inputs. This process typically involves two stages: identifying the layer to edit and performing the parameter update. Intuitively, different queries may localize knowledge at different depths of the model, resulting in different sample-wise editin…
items.sm: Identifies fixed model layers through gradient analysis that approach query-specific optimal performance for knowledge editing and generalize to unseen queries.

items.t: Uncovering Context Reliance in Unstructured Knowledge Editing
items.a: Zisheng Zhou, Mengqi Zhang, Shiguang Wu, Xiaotian Ye, Chi Zhang, Zhumin Chen, Pengjie Ren
items.x: Editing Large language models (LLMs) with real-world, unstructured knowledge is essential for correcting and updating their internal parametric knowledge. items.sm: Introduces a graph representation and weight-space architecture for Kolmogorov-Arnold networks that respects parameter permutation symmetries and can reproduce their forward computations.

items.t: MolEdit: Knowledge Editing for Multimodal Molecule Language Models

items.t: PRISM: Parallel Residual Iterative Sequence Model

items.t: LARV: Data-Free Layer-wise Adaptive Rescaling Veneer for Model Merging
items.a: Xinyu Wang, Ke Deng, Fei Dou, Jinbo Bi, Jin Lu
items.x: Model merging aims to combine multiple fine-tuned models into a single multi-task model without access to training data. Existing task-vector merging methods such as TIES, TSV-M, and Iso-C/CTS differ in their aggregation rules but treat all layers nearly uniformly. This assumption overlooks the strong layer-wise heterogeneity in large vision transformers, where shallow layers are sensitive to interference while deepe…
items.sm: Rescales task updates by layer before model merging to reduce shallow-layer interference and strengthen deeper-layer contributions without training or data.

items.t: Simple LLM Baselines are Competitive for Model Diffing
items.a: Elias Kempf, Simon Schrodi, Bartosz Cywiński, Thomas Brox, Neel Nanda, Arthur Conmy
items.x: Standard LLM evaluations only test capabilities or dispositions that evaluators designed them for, missing unexpected differences such as behavioral shifts between model revisions or emergent misaligned tendencies. Model diffing addresses this limitation by automatically surfacing systematic behavioral differences. Recent approaches include LLM-based methods that generate natural language descriptions and sparse auto…
items.sm: Proposes evaluation metrics for model diffing and finds an improved language-model baseline comparable to sparse-autoencoder methods while producing more abstract descriptions.

items.t: Model soups need only one ingredient
items.a: Alireza Abdollahpoorrostam, Nikolaos Dimitriadis, Adam Hazimeh, Pascal Frossard
items.x: Fine-tuning large pre-trained models on a target distribution often improves in-distribution (ID) accuracy, but at the cost of out-of-distribution (OOD) robustness as representations specialize to the fine-tuning data. Weight-space ensembling methods, such as Model Soups, mitigate this effect by averaging multiple checkpoints, but they are computationally prohibitive, requiring the training and storage of dozens of f…
items.sm: Processes a single fine-tuned checkpoint using singular value decomposition to balance target-distribution accuracy and robustness without additional data or hyperparameters.

items.t: Step-resolved data attribution for looped transformers
items.a: Georgios A. Kaissis, David Mildenberger, Juan Felipe Gomez, Martin J. Menten, Eleni Triantafillou
items.x: We study how individual training examples shape the internal computation of looped transformers, where a shared block is applied for $τ$ recurrent iterations to enable latent reasoning. Existing training-data influence estimators such as TracIn yield a single scalar score that aggregates over all loop iterations, obscuring when during the recurrent computation a training example matters. We introduce \textit{Step-Dec…
items.sm: Decomposes training-example influence across looped Transformer iterations and uses TensorSketch to estimate these trajectories without materializing per-example gradients.

items.t: Wangzzzzzzzz/OTE-SE-Alignment

items.sm: Provides OTE–SE Alignment code for research examining regularization in sequential knowledge editing of large language models.

items.sm: Provides code using gradient-sign masking to transfer task vectors across pretrained models.

items.t: Steer2Edit: From Activation Steering to Component-Level Editing
items.a: Chung-En Sun, Ge Yan, Zimo Wang, Tsui-Wei Weng
items.sm: Converts activation steering vectors into diagnostic signals for targeted rank-one weight edits, aiming to improve behavioral control while preserving model utility.

items.t: Sparsity-Aware Evolution for Model Merging
items.a: Huan Zhang, Yanjian Zhang, Guillaume Wisniewski, Nadi Tomeh, Bang Liu
items.x: We propose a sparsity-aware evolutionary (SAE) framework for model merging that involves iterative pruning-merging cycles to act as a novel mutation operator. We incorporate the sparsity constraints into the score function, which steers the evolutionary process to favor more sparse models, in addition to other conventional performance scores. Interestingly, the by-product of \textit{competition} for sparsity introduc…
items.sm: Uses repeated pruning and merging within evolutionary search, rewarding sparsity alongside performance to improve model merging reliability.

items.t: GOT-Edit: Geometry-Aware Generic Object Tracking via Online Model Editing
items.a: Shih‐Fang Chen, Jun-Cheng Chen, I‐Hong Jhuo, Yen-Yu Lin
items.x: Human perception for effective object tracking in 2D video streams arises from the implicit use of prior 3D knowledge and semantic reasoning. In contrast, most generic object tracking (GOT) methods primarily rely on 2D features of the target and its surroundings, while neglecting 3D geometric cues, making them susceptible to partial occlusion, distractors, and variations in geometry and appearance. To address this li…
items.sm: Edits object trackers online to incorporate geometric cues inferred from a few video frames using a pretrained geometry model and null-space constraints.

items.sm: Provides a federated hypernetwork approach using hyperbolic directional diffusion.

items.sm: Implements Sakana AI's Fast-weight Product Key Memory method.

items.t: Reverse-Engineering Model Editing on Language Models
items.a: Zhiyu Sun, Minrui Luo, Yu Wang, Zhili Chen, Tianxing He
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) are pretrained on corpora containing trillions of tokens and, therefore, inevitably memorize sensitive information. Locate-then-edit methods, as a mainstream paradigm of model editing, offer a promising solution by modifying model parameters without retraining. However, in this work, we reveal a critical vulnerability of this paradigm: the parameter updates inadvertently serve as a side c…
items.sm: Introduces an attack that exploits low-rank model-editing updates to recover edited information, including subjects identified through spectral analysis.

items.t: AdamZvara/DIP_Diversity_datasets

items.x: Dataset creation for Diversity tests of ROME/MEMIT
items.sm: Creates datasets for testing the diversity of ROME and MEMIT knowledge edits.

items.a: TTrapper
items.x: Train a hypernetwork that generates the weights for neural cellular automata and then explore the latent space of NCAs using music
items.sm: Trains a hypernetwork to generate neural cellular automaton weights and uses music to explore their latent space.

items.t: Fine-Grained Model Merging via Modular Expert Recombination
items.a: Haiyun Qiu, Xingyu Wu, Liang Feng, Kay Chen Tan
items.x: Model merging constructs versatile models by integrating task-specific models without requiring labeled data or expensive joint retraining. Although recent methods improve adaptability to heterogeneous tasks by generating customized merged models for each instance, they face two critical limitations. First, the instance-specific merged models lack reusability, restricting the exploitation of high-quality merging conf…
items.sm: Proposes modular expert recombination for fine-grained model merging to address limited reuse of instance-specific merges and differing mergeability across model components.

items.t: ToadResearch/tracr
items.a: ToadResearch
items.x: OCR web viewer + TUI
items.sm: Provides web and terminal interfaces for viewing optical character recognition output.

items.t: SHINE: A Scalable In-Context Hypernetwork for Mapping Context to LoRA in a Single Pass
items.a: Yewei Liu, Xiyuan Wang, Yansheng Mao, Yoav Gelbery, Haggai Maron, Muhan Zhang
items.x: We propose SHINE (Scalable Hyper In-context NEtwork), a scalable hypernetwork that can map diverse meaningful contexts into high-quality LoRA adapters for large language models (LLMs). By reusing the frozen LLM's own parameters in an in-context hypernetwork design and introducing architectural innovations, SHINE overcomes key limitations of prior hypernetworks and achieves strong expressive power with a relatively sm…
items.sm: Generates LoRA adapters from context in one forward pass using a hypernetwork that reuses frozen language-model parameters, enabling questions without accessing that context again.

items.t: Dynamics-aligned shared hypernetworks for zero-shot actuator inversion
items.a: Jan Benad, Pradeep Kumar Banerjee, Frank Röder, Nihat Ay, Martin V. Butz, Manfred Eppe
items.sm: Uses a dynamics-trained hypernetwork to generate adapters shared across reinforcement learning components, supporting adaptation when hidden context reverses actuator effects.

items.t: Dynamics-Aligned Shared Hypernetworks for Contextual RL under Discontinuous Shifts
items.a: Jan Benad, Pradeep Banerjee, Frank Röder, Nihat Ay, Martin V. Butz, Manfred Eppe
items.x: Zero-shot generalization in contextual reinforcement learning remains a core challenge, particularly when the context is latent and must be inferred from data. A canonical failure mode arises when latent context discontinuously changes how actions affect the environment, requiring incompatible control responses across contexts. We propose DMA*-SH, a framework where a single hypernetwork, trained solely via dynamics p…
items.sm: Uses a dynamics-trained hypernetwork to share adapters across dynamics, policy, and value models, supporting adaptation to abrupt changes in action effects.

items.t: DARWIN: Dynamic Agentically Rewriting Self-Improving Network
items.a: Henry Jiang
items.x: DARWIN is an evolutionary GPT model, utilizing a genetic-algorithm like optimization structure with several independent GPT agents being trained individually using unique training code. Each iteration, the GPT models are prompted to modify the training code of one another in an attempt to improve their performance in a mutation-like manner, and the best GPT agents are then benchmarked and selected for the next iterat…
items.sm: Uses GPT agents to revise one another’s training code, selects better performers through evolutionary optimization, and records changes in persistent memory.

items.t: Orthogonal Model Merging
items.a: Sihan Yang, Kexuan Shi, Zhifeng Li
items.x: Merging finetuned Large Language Models (LLMs) has become increasingly important for integrating diverse capabilities into a single unified model. However, prevailing model merging methods rely on linear arithmetic in Euclidean space, which often destroys the intrinsic geometric properties of pretrained weights, such as hyperspherical energy. To address this, we propose Orthogonal Model Merging (OrthoMerge), a method…
items.sm: Merges task-specific orthogonal adaptations through Lie algebra representations to preserve pretrained weight geometry while accounting for adaptation direction and strength.

items.t: Bagging-Based Model Merging for Robust General Text Embeddings
items.a: Hengran Zhang, Keping Bi, Jiafeng Guo, Jiaming Zhang, Wenbo Yang, Daiting Shi, Xueqi Cheng
items.x: General-purpose text embedding models underpin a wide range of NLP and information retrieval applications, and are typically trained on large-scale multi-task corpora to encourage broad generalization. However, it remains unclear how different multi-task training strategies compare in practice, and how to efficiently adapt embedding models as new domains and data types continually emerge. In this work, we present a s…
items.sm: Compares multitask training and model merging strategies for text embeddings, finding that mixing examples across tasks consistently delivers the strongest overall performance.

items.t: When Shared Knowledge Hurts: Spectral Over-Accumulation in Model Merging
items.a: Yayuan Li, Ze Peng, Jian Zhang, Jintao Guo, Yue Duan, Yinghuan Shi
items.x: Model merging combines multiple fine-tuned models into a single model by adding their weight updates, providing a lightweight alternative to retraining. Existing methods primarily target resolving conflicts between task updates, leaving the failure mode of over-counting shared knowledge unaddressed. We show that when tasks share aligned spectral directions (i.e., overlapping singular vectors), a simple linear combina…
items.sm: Identifies repeated accumulation of shared weight directions during model merging and proposes rescaling inflated singular values to improve merged models without training or data.

items.t: Transport and Merge: Cross-Architecture Merging for Large Language Models
items.a: Chenhang Cui, Binyun Yang, Fei Shen, Yuxin Chen, Jingnan Zheng, Xiang Wang, An Zhang, Tat-Seng Chua
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) achieve strong capabilities by scaling model capacity and training data, yet many real-world deployments rely on smaller models trained or adapted from low-resource data. This gap motivates the need for mechanisms to transfer knowledge from large, high-resource models to smaller, low-resource targets. While model merging provides an effective transfer mechanism, most existing approaches a…
items.sm: Uses optimal transport to align neurons across different language model architectures and guide weight merging from larger models into smaller targets.

items.x: Official code Implementation of "When Shared Knowledge Hurts: Spectral Over-Accumulation in Model Merging" (ICML-26)
items.sm: Provides code studying how accumulated shared knowledge can harm model merging through spectral effects.

items.sm: Uses a hypernetwork to distill Qwen3-Coder teacher trajectories into LoRA adaptations.

items.t: Linear Model Merging Unlocks Simple and Scalable Multimodal Data Mixture Optimization
items.a: Davide Berasi, Matteo Farina, Massimiliano Mancini, Elisa Ricci
items.x: Selecting the best data mixture is critical for successful Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) of Multimodal Large Language Models. However, determining the optimal mixture weights across multiple domain-specific datasets remains a significant bottleneck due to the combinatorial search space and the high cost associated with even a single training run. This is the so-called Data Mixture Optimization (DMO) problem. On the ot…
items.sm: Uses weighted combinations of domain-specific multimodal models to estimate how different training data mixtures will perform, reducing the need for repeated training.

items.t: Conflict-Resolving and Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Generalized Knowledge Editing with Multiple Updates
items.a: Duy Nguyen, Hanqi Xiao, Archiki Prasad, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Hyunji Lee, Mohit Bansal
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) rely on internal knowledge to solve many downstream tasks, making it crucial to keep them up to date. Since full retraining is expensive, prior work has explored efficient alternatives such as model editing and parameter-efficient fine-tuning. However, these approaches often break down in practice due to poor generalization across inputs, limited stability, and knowledge conflict. To addr…
items.sm: Introduces a parameter-efficient knowledge editing framework that reduces loss curvature and separates new from prior knowledge to improve generalization, stability, and conflict handling.

items.t: UnHype: CLIP-Guided Hypernetworks for Dynamic LoRA Unlearning
items.a: Piotr Iwo Wójcik, Maksym Petrenko, Wojciech Gromski, Przemysław Spurek, Maciej Zieba
items.x: Recent advances in large-scale diffusion models have intensified concerns about their potential misuse, particularly in generating realistic yet harmful or socially disruptive content. This challenge has spurred growing interest in effective machine unlearning, the process of selectively removing specific knowledge or concepts from a model without compromising its overall generative capabilities. Among various approa…
items.sm: Proposes CLIP-guided hypernetworks for dynamically generating LoRA updates that remove selected concepts from diffusion models.

items.t: BerasiDavide/mLLMs_merging_4_DMO
items.a: BerasiDavide
items.x: Official implementation of the paper "Linear Model Merging Unlocks Simple and Scalable Multimodal Data Mixture Optimization".
items.sm: Implements linear model merging for optimizing multimodal training data mixtures.

items.t: Beyond Local Edits: Embedding-Virtualized Knowledge for Broader Evaluation and Preservation of Model Editing
items.a: Shuainan Liu, Xuanang Chen, Ben He, Le Sun
items.x: Knowledge editing methods for large language models are commonly evaluated using predefined benchmarks that assess edited facts together with a limited set of related or neighboring knowledge. While effective, such evaluations remain confined to finite, dataset-bounded samples, leaving the broader impact of editing on the model's knowledge system insufficiently understood. To address this gap, we introduce Embedding-…
items.sm: Introduces embedding perturbations and a benchmark to evaluate broader knowledge changes caused by model editing beyond explicitly annotated facts.

items.t: Mixture-of-Top-k Attention: Efficient Attention via Scalable Fast Weights
items.a: Qishuai Wen, Zhiyuan Huang, Xianghan Meng, Wei He, Chunguang Li
items.x: The vanilla self-attention mechanism in Transformers can be viewed as a two-layer fast-weight MLP, whose weights are dynamically induced by inputs and whose hidden dimension is equal to the sequence length $N$. As the context extends, the expressive capacity of such an $N$-width MLP increases, but it becomes unscalable for extremely long sequences. Recently, this fast-weight perspective has motivated the Mixture-of-E…
items.sm: Organizes efficient attention methods around routing and compressing fast weights, and proposes Mixture-of-Top-k Attention for scalable sequence processing.

items.t: On the Expressive Power of Permutation-Equivariant Weight-Space Networks
items.a: Adir Dayan, Yam Eitan, Haggai Maron
items.x: Weight-space learning studies neural architectures that operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. Motivated by the growing availability of pretrained models, recent work has demonstrated the effectiveness of weight-space networks across a wide range of tasks. SOTA weight-space networks rely on permutation-equivariant designs to improve generalization. However, this may negatively affect expressive …
items.sm: Develops a theoretical framework for analyzing what permutation-equivariant networks operating on neural network weights can represent.

items.t: Edit Knowledge, Not Just Facts via Multi-Step Reasoning over Background Stories
items.a: Ya Gao, Kalle Kujanpää, Pekka Marttinen, Harri Valpola B, Alexander Ilin
items.v: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
items.x: Enabling artificial intelligence systems, particularly large language models, to update knowledge and flexibly apply it during reasoning remains a central challenge.Existing knowledge editing approaches emphasize atomic facts, improving factual recall but often failing to integrate updated information into a coherent framework usable across contexts.In this work, we argue that knowledge update is fundamentally a reas…
items.sm: Argues that knowledge updates require reasoning and proposes training with contextual background stories that integrate new information into multistep tasks.

items.t: On the Robustness of Knowledge Editing for Detoxification
items.a: Ming Dong, Shiyi Tang, Ziyan Peng, Guanyi Chen, Tingting He
items.v: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
items.x: Knowledge-Editing-based (KE-based) detoxification has emerged as a promising approach for mitigating harmful behaviours in Large Language Models.Existing evaluations, however, largely rely on automatic toxicity classifiers, implicitly assuming that reduced toxicity scores reflect genuine behavioural suppression.In this work, we propose a robustness-oriented evaluation framework for KE-based detoxification that examin…
items.sm: Evaluates knowledge editing for detoxification, finding misleading toxicity reductions from degraded generation and weaker effectiveness when editing multiple unsafe behaviors together.

items.t: LoopViT: Scaling Visual ARC with Looped Transformers
items.a: Wen-Jie Shu, Xuerui Qiu, Rui-Jie Zhu, Harold Haodong Chen, Yexin Liu, Harry Yang
items.v: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP (Findings of EMNLP)
items.x: Recent ARC-AGI systems have shown that pure vision can solve abstract grid reasoning without language backbones, but most strong models still rely on fixed-depth feed-forward computation.We study whether recurrent computation is a better scaling axis for this setting.We propose Loop-ViT, a vision-native recurrent model that reuses a weight-tied Hybrid Block across multiple steps, with local convolutions for image-tok…
items.sm: Introduces a recurrent vision transformer with adaptive stopping that achieves 65.8% accuracy on ARC-AGI-1 using 18 million parameters.

items.t: SpiralFormer: Looped Transformers Can Learn Hierarchical Dependencies via Multi-Resolution Recursion
items.a: Chengting Yu, Xiaobo Shu, Yadao Wang, Yizhen Zhang, Haoyi Wu, You Wu, Rujiao Long, Ziheng Chen
items.v: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
items.x: Recursive (looped) Transformers decouple computational depth from parameter depth by repeatedly applying shared layers, providing an explicit architectural primitive for iterative refinement and latent reasoning.However, early looped Transformers often underperform nonrecursive baselines of equal compute.While recent literature has introduced more effective recursion mechanisms to mitigate this gap, existing architec…
items.sm: Proposes a looped transformer that processes multiple representation resolutions, with probing evidence suggesting different iterations specialize in hierarchical dependencies.

items.t: Decouple Searching from Training: Scaling Data Mixing via Model Merging for Large Language Model Pre-training
items.a: Shengrui Li, Fei Zhao, Kaiyan Zhao, Jiaqi Ye, Haifeng Liu, Fangcheng Shi, Zheyong Xie, Yao Hu
items.x: Determining an effective data mixture is a key factor in Large Language Model (LLM) pre-training, where models must balance general competence with proficiency on hard tasks such as math and code. However, identifying an optimal mixture remains an open challenge, as existing approaches either rely on unreliable tiny-scale proxy experiments or require prohibitively expensive large-scale exploration. To address this, w…
items.sm: Predicts useful pretraining data ratios by merging models trained on individual datasets, allowing candidate mixtures to be evaluated without additional training.

items.t: LatentTrack: Sequential Weight Generation via Latent Filtering
items.a: Omer Haq
items.x: We introduce LatentTrack (LT), a sequential neural architecture for online probabilistic prediction under nonstationary dynamics. LT performs causal Bayesian filtering in a low-dimensional latent space and uses a lightweight hypernetwork to generate predictive model parameters at each time step, enabling constant-time online adaptation without per-step gradient updates. At each time step, a learned latent model predi…
items.sm: Combines Bayesian filtering in a compact latent space with a hypernetwork that generates prediction weights, enabling online adaptation without per-step gradient updates.

items.t: Lucius-lsr/DeMix

items.x: The offical implementation of DeMix (Decouple Searching from Training: Scaling Data Mixing via Model Merging for Large Language Model Pre-training)
items.sm: Uses model merging to separate data mixture search from training for large language model pretraining.

items.t: AutoMerge: Search-Based Model Merging Framework for Effective Model Reuse
items.a: You Lu, Jiyang Zhang, Bihuan Chen, Chaofeng Sha, Dingji Wang, Xin Peng
items.x: Software reuse has long been recognized as a critical and widely studied topic in software engineering, offering substantial benefits in reducing development costs, improving software quality, and enhancing operational efficiency. This paradigm extends into deep learning through model reuse. Recently, model merging has emerged in the domain of large language models (LLMs) as a training-free approach that takes multip…
items.sm: Studies model merging across architectures and application domains and introduces a search-based framework for reusing trained models.

items.t: Norm Anchors Make Model Edits Last
items.a: Mingda Liu, Zhenghan Zhu, Ze'an Miao, Katsuki Fujisawa
items.x: Sequential Locate-and-Edit (L&E) model editing can fail abruptly after many edits. We identify and formalize this failure as a positive norm-feedback loop, in which solved value vectors and edited MLP weights progressively amplify each other, degrading edit quality and eventually collapsing model capabilities. Our analysis shows that this feedback can yield approximately exponential norm growth under standard L&E dyn…
items.sm: Identifies runaway weight growth during sequential model editing and proposes reference-based rescaling that extends editing longevity by more than fourfold.

items.t: HyperSBINN: A Hypernetwork-Enhanced Systems Biology-Informed Neural Network for Efficient Drug Cardiosafety Assessment
items.a: Inass Soukarieh, Gerhard Heßler, Hervé Minoux, Marcel Mohr, Friedemann Schmidt, Jan Wenzel, Pierre Barbillon, Hugo Gangloff
items.x: Mathematical modeling in systems toxicology enables a comprehensive understanding of the effects of pharmaceutical substances on cardiac health. However, the complexity of these models limits their widespread application in early drug discovery. In this article, we introduce a novel approach to solving parameterized models of cardiac action potentials (CAPs) by combining meta-learning techniques with systems biology-…
items.sm: Combines hypernetworks with biology-informed neural networks to predict drug effects on cardiac action potentials faster than traditional differential equation solvers.

items.t: Ensuring Semantics in Weights of Implicit Neural Representations through the Implicit Function Theorem
items.a: Tianming Qiu, Christos Sonis, Hao Shen
items.x: Weight Space Learning (WSL), which frames neural network weights as a data modality, is an emerging field with potential for tasks like meta-learning or transfer learning. Particularly, Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) provide a convenient testbed, where each set of weights determines the corresponding individual data sample as a mapping from coordinates to contextual values. So far, a precise theoretical expla…
items.sm: Uses the implicit function theorem to connect data semantics with neural representation weights and evaluates hypernetwork-generated representations on classification tasks.

items.t: Behemoth: Benchmarking Unlearning in LLMs Using Fully Synthetic Data
items.a: Eugenia Iofinova, Dan Alistarh
items.x: As artificial neural networks, and specifically large language models, have improved rapidly in capabilities and quality, they have increasingly been deployed in real-world applications, from customer service to Google search, despite the fact that they frequently make factually incorrect or undesirable statements. This trend has inspired practical and academic interest in model editing, that is, in adjusting the wei…
items.sm: Introduces a benchmark using fully synthetic data to evaluate unlearning in large language models.

items.sm: Implements attribution-controlled knowledge editing for factual recall involving multiple reasoning steps.

items.sm: Uses hypernetworks to learn adaptive guidance, navigation, and control across multiple tasks.

items.t: Per-parameter Task Arithmetic for Unlearning in Large Language Models
items.a: Chengyi Cai, Zesheng Ye, Jiangchao Yao, Jianzhong Qi, Bo Han, Xiaolu Zhang, Feng Liu, Jun Zhou
items.x: In large language model (LLM) unlearning, private information is required to be removed. Task arithmetic unlearns by subtracting a specific task vector (TV)--defined as the parameter difference between a privacy-information-tuned model and the original model. While efficient, it can cause over-forgetting by disrupting parameters essential for retaining other information. Motivated by the observation that each paramet…
items.sm: Rescales each parameter's unlearning update using gradients or Fisher information to balance removing private information against preserving other knowledge.

items.t: Demystifying Mergeability: Interpretable Properties to Predict Model Merging Success
items.a: Luca Zhou, Bo Zhao, Rose Yu, Emanuele Rodolà
items.x: Model merging combines knowledge from separately fine-tuned models, yet the factors driving its success remain poorly understood. While recent work treats mergeability as an intrinsic property of the models, we show with an architecture-agnostic framework that it fundamentally depends on both the merging method and the partner tasks. Using L1-regularized linear optimization over a set of interpretable pairwise metric…
items.sm: Finds that model merging success depends on the merging method and partner tasks, with gradient alignment providing a consistent predictive signal.

items.t: A Unified Generalization Framework for Model Merging: Trade-offs, Non-Linearity, and Scaling Laws
items.a: Qinglun Li, Anke Tang, Miao Zhang, Mengzhu Wang, Quanjun Yin, Li Shen
items.x: Model merging efficiently aggregates capabilities from multiple fine-tuned models into a single one, operating purely in parameter space without original data or expensive re-computation. Despite empirical successes, a unified theory for its effectiveness under heterogeneous finetuning hyperparameters (e.g., varying learning rates, batch sizes) remains missing. Existing federated learning theories focus purely on opt…
items.sm: Develops a stability-based theory separating optimization and generalization errors in model merging when source models use different fine-tuning settings.

items.t: FRISM: Fine-Grained Reasoning Injection via Subspace-Level Model Merging for Vision-Language Models
items.a: Chenyu Huang, Peng Ye, Xudong Tan, Jinhan Mu, Shenghe Zheng, Li Shen, Tao Chen
items.x: Efficiently enhancing the reasoning capabilities of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) by merging them with Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) has emerged as a promising direction. However, existing methods typically operate at a coarse-grained layer level, which often leads to a trade-off between injecting reasoning capabilities and preserving visual capabilities. To address this limitation, we propose FRISM (Fine-grained Rea…
items.sm: Transfers reasoning capabilities into vision-language models by learning separate scaling factors for singular-vector subspaces, aiming to preserve visual capabilities.

items.t: Making Models Unmergeable via Scaling-Sensitive Loss Landscape
items.a: Minwoo Jang, Hoyoung Kim, Jabin Koo, Jungseul Ok
items.x: The rise of model hubs has made it easier to access reusable model components, making model merging a practical tool for combining capabilities. Yet, this modularity also creates a governance gap: downstream users can recompose released weights into unauthorized mixtures that bypass safety alignment or licensing terms. Because existing defenses are largely post-hoc and architecture-specific, they provide inconsistent…
items.sm: Proposes fine-tuning models to retain standalone performance while becoming sensitive to weight rescaling, aiming to hinder unauthorized model merging.

items.t: Molecular Representations in Implicit Functional Space via Hyper-Networks
items.a: Zehong Wang, Xiaolong Han, Qi Yang, Xiangru Tang, Fang Wu, Xiaoguang Guo, Weixiang Sun, Tianyi Ma
items.x: Molecular representations fundamentally shape how machine learning systems reason about molecular structure and physical properties. Most existing approaches adopt a discrete pipeline: molecules are encoded as sequences, graphs, or point clouds, mapped to fixed-dimensional embeddings, and then used for task-specific prediction. This paradigm treats molecules as discrete objects, despite their intrinsically continuous…
items.sm: Represents molecules as continuous functions over three-dimensional space and introduces MolField to implement this approach using hypernetworks.

items.t: Neuro-Memristive Hypernetworks for Self-Evolving Artificial Intelligence: A Hardware-Algorithm Co-Evolution Paradigm
items.a: Rajneet Kaur, Gitanjali Gupta, Vedika Mishra, Muskan Pandey

items.t: Generalizable Multimodal Large Language Model Editing via Invariant Trajectory Learning
items.a: Jiajie Su, Haoyuan Wang, Xiaohua Feng, Yunshan Ma, Xiaobo Xia, Yuyuan Li, Xiaolin Zheng, Jianmao Xiao
items.x: Knowledge editing emerges as a crucial technique for efficiently correcting incorrect or outdated knowledge in large language models (LLM). Existing editing methods rely on a rigid mapping from parameter or module modifications to output, which causes the generalization limitation in Multimodal LLM (MLLM). In this paper, we reformulate MLLM editing as an out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization problem, where the goa…
items.sm: Frames multimodal knowledge editing as generalization across unfamiliar inputs and proposes invariant trajectory learning to improve reliability, locality, and generalization.

items.t: MergeMix: Optimizing Mid-Training Data Mixtures via Learnable Model Merging
items.a: Jiapeng Wang, Changxin Tian, Kunlong Chen, Ziqi Liu, Jiaxin Mao, Wayne Xin Zhao, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou
items.x: Optimizing data mixtures is essential for unlocking the full potential of large language models (LLMs), yet identifying the optimal composition remains computationally prohibitive due to reliance on heuristic trials or expensive proxy training. To address this, we introduce \textbf{MergeMix}, a novel approach that efficiently determines optimal data mixing ratios by repurposing model merging weights as a high-fidelit…
items.sm: Learns merging weights for briefly trained domain experts to select mid-training data mixtures, reporting performance comparable to manual tuning at lower search cost.

items.t: CLM-Bench: Benchmarking and Analyzing Cross-lingual Misalignment of LLMs in Knowledge Editing
items.a: Yucheng Hu, Wei Zhou, Juesi Xiao
items.x: Knowledge Editing (KE) has emerged as a promising paradigm for updating facts in Large Language Models (LLMs) without retraining. However, progress in Multilingual Knowledge Editing (MKE) is currently hindered by biased evaluation frameworks. We observe that existing MKE benchmarks are typically constructed by mechanically translating English-centric datasets into target languages (e.g., English-to-Chinese). This app…
items.sm: Introduces 1,010 Chinese cultural fact pairs with English counterparts to evaluate cross-language knowledge editing while reducing biases from translated English benchmarks.

items.t: Are We Evaluating the Edit Locality of LLM Model Editing Properly?
items.a: Wei Liu, Haomei Xu, Hongkai Liu, Zhiying Deng, Ruixuan Li, Heng Huang, Yee Whye Teh, Wee Sun Lee
items.x: Model editing has recently emerged as a popular paradigm for efficiently updating knowledge in LLMs. A central desideratum of updating knowledge is to balance editing efficacy, i.e., the successful injection of target knowledge, and specificity (also known as edit locality), i.e., the preservation of existing non-target knowledge. However, we find that existing specificity evaluation protocols are inadequate for this…
items.sm: Identifies weaknesses in evaluating whether language model edits preserve unrelated knowledge and proposes a more sensitive evaluation protocol.

items.t: SonoEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Pronunciation Correction in LLM-Based TTS
items.a: Ayush Pratap Singh, Harshit Singh, Nityanand Mathur, Akshat Mandloi, Sudarshan Kamath
items.x: Neural text-to-speech (TTS) systems systematically mispronounce low-resource proper nouns, particularly non-English names, brands, and geographic locations, due to their underrepresentation in predominantly English training corpora. Existing solutions typically rely on expensive multilingual data collection, supervised finetuning, or manual phonetic annotation, which limits the deployment of TTS systems in linguistic…
items.sm: Introduces SonoEdit, which corrects specific word pronunciations in speech synthesis models through a single parameter update designed to preserve other behavior.

items.t: MMGRid: Navigating Temporal-aware and Cross-domain Generative Recommendation via Model Merging
items.a: Tianjun Wei, Enneng Yang, Yingpeng Du, Huizhong Guo, Jie Zhang, Zhu Sun
items.x: Model merging (MM) offers an efficient mechanism for integrating multiple specialized models without access to original training data or costly retraining. While MM has demonstrated success in domains like computer vision, its role in recommender systems (RSs) remains largely unexplored. Recently, Generative Recommendation (GR) has emerged as a new paradigm in RSs, characterized by rapidly growing model scales and su…
items.sm: Studies merging generative recommendation models specialized for different time periods and application domains, proposing a unified framework for combining them.

items.t: HyperAlign: Hypernetwork for Efficient Test-Time Alignment of Diffusion Models
items.a: Xin Xie, Jiaxian Guo, Dong Gong
items.x: Diffusion model alignment aims to bridge the gap between generated outputs and human preferences by enhancing both semantic consistency with textual prompts and overall visual quality. Existing alignment methods face a challenging trade-off: test-time approaches enable input-specific adaptability but introduce significant computational overhead and tend to under-optimize, while fine-tuning approaches risk reward over…
items.sm: Introduces HyperAlign, a hypernetwork that generates adaptive weight updates during diffusion sampling to improve alignment with prompts and target rewards.

items.t: Learning to Discover at Test Time
items.a: Mert Yüksekgönül, Daniel Koceja, Xinhao Li, Federico Bianchi, Jed McCaleb, Xiaolong Wang, Jan Kautz, Yejin Choi
items.x: How can we use AI to discover a new state of the art for a scientific problem? Prior work in test-time scaling, such as AlphaEvolve, performs search by prompting a frozen LLM. We perform reinforcement learning at test time, so the LLM can continue to train, but now with experience specific to the test problem. This form of continual learning is quite special, because its goal is to produce one great solution rather t…
items.sm: Introduces test-time reinforcement learning that trains language models on individual scientific problems, prioritizing the search for one strong solution.

items.t: HyperNet-Adaptation for Diffusion-Based Test Case Generation
items.a: Oliver Weißl, Vincenzo Riccio, Severin Kacianka, Andrea Stocco
items.x: The increasing deployment of deep learning systems requires systematic evaluation of their reliability in real-world scenarios. Traditional gradient-based adversarial attacks introduce small perturbations that rarely correspond to realistic failures and mainly assess robustness rather than functional behavior. Generative test generation methods offer an alternative but are often limited to simple datasets or constrai…
items.sm: Introduces HyNeA, which uses hypernetworks to control diffusion image generation for targeted testing of deep learning systems without requiring a dataset.

items.t: Multi-Sensor Matching with HyperNetworks
items.a: Eli Passov, Nathan S. Netanyahu, Yosi Keller
items.x: Hypernetworks are models that generate or modulate the weights of another network. They provide a flexible mechanism for injecting context and task conditioning and have proven broadly useful across diverse applications without significant increases in model size. We leverage hypernetworks to improve multimodal patch matching by introducing a lightweight descriptor-learning architecture that augments a Siamese CNN wi…
items.sm: Combines hypernetworks and modality-specific normalization to improve image patch matching across sensors while retaining efficient inference.
