items.sm: Presents HyConEx, a hypernetwork classifier that provides counterfactual explanations for tabular data.

items.t: Energy-Entropy Regularization: The True Power of Minimal Looped Transformers
items.a: Wai‐Lun Lam
items.x: Recent research suggests that looped Transformers have superior reasoning capabilities compared to standard deep architectures. Current approaches to training single-head looped architectures on benchmark tasks frequently fail or yield suboptimal performance due to a highly non-convex and irregular loss landscape. In these settings, optimization often stagnates in poor local minima and saddle points of the loss lands…
items.sm: Proposes a training framework using Tsallis entropy and Hamiltonian dynamics to improve optimization of single-head looped transformers.

items.t: SimMerge: Learning to Select Merge Operators from Similarity Signals
items.a: Oliver Bolton, Aakanksha, Arash Ahmadian, Sara Hooker, Marzieh Fadaee, Beyza Ermiş
items.x: Model merging combines multiple models into a single model with aggregated capabilities, making it a powerful tool for large language model (LLM) development. However, scaling model merging is challenging: performance depends on the choice of merge operator, model subset, and merge order, often requiring expensive merge-and-evaluate searches. In this work, we introduce SimMerge, a predictive merge-selection method th…
items.sm: Introduces SimMerge, which predicts successful model merges from inexpensive similarity measurements to select merge operators, model subsets, and merging order.

items.t: Knowledge-Embedded and Hypernetwork-Guided Few-Shot Substation Meter Defect Image Generation Method
items.a: Jackie Alex, Justin Petter
items.x: Substation meters play a critical role in monitoring and ensuring the stable operation of power grids, yet their detection of cracks and other physical defects is often hampered by a severe scarcity of annotated samples. items.sm: Combines equipment-specific knowledge and hypernetwork guidance in Stable Diffusion to generate controllable substation meter defect images from limited examples.

items.t: Evaluating Cross-Lingual Unlearning in Multilingual Language Models
items.a: Tyler Lizzo, Larry Heck
items.x: We present the first comprehensive evaluation of cross-lingual unlearning in multilingual LLMs. Using translated TOFU benchmarks in seven language/script variants, we test major unlearning algorithms and show that most fail to remove facts outside the training language, even when utility remains high. items.t: HAPS: Hierarchical LLM Routing with Joint Architecture and Parameter Search
items.a: Zihang Tian, Rui Li, Jingsen Zhang, Xiaohe Bo, Wei Huo, Xu Chen
items.x: Large language model (LLM) routing aims to exploit the specialized strengths of different LLMs for diverse tasks. items.t: On the Limitations of Rank-One Model Editing in Answering Multi-hop Questions
items.a: Zhiyuan He, Binghan Chen, Tianxiang Xiong, Ziyang Sun, Mozhao Zhu, Xi Chen

items.x: Transformers excel empirically on tasks that process well-formed inputs according to some grammar, such as natural language and code. However, it remains unclear how they can process grammatical syntax. In fact, under standard complexity conjectures, standard transformers cannot recognize context-free languages (CFLs), a canonical formalism to describe syntax, or even regular languages, a subclass of CFLs. items.sm: Shows that looped transformers can recognize all context-free languages using logarithmically many looping layers and padding that grows with the sixth power of input length.

items.t: REE-TTT: Highly Adaptive Radar Echo Extrapolation Based on Test-Time Training
items.a: Xin Di, Xinglin Piao, Fei Wang, Guodong Jing, Yong Zhang
items.x: Precipitation nowcasting is critically important for meteorological forecasting. Deep learning-based Radar Echo Extrapolation (REE) has become a predominant nowcasting approach, yet it suffers from poor generalization due to its reliance on high-quality local training data and static model parameters, limiting its applicability across diverse regions and extreme events. To overcome this, we propose REE-TTT, a novel m…
items.sm: Introduces REE-TTT, which adapts radar echo extrapolation models during inference using spatial and temporal attention to handle changing precipitation patterns.

items.t: Fast-weight Product Key Memory
items.a: Tianyu Zhao, Llion Jones
items.x: Sequence modeling layers in modern language models typically face a trade-off between storage capacity and computational efficiency. While softmax attention offers unbounded storage at prohibitive quadratic cost, linear variants are more efficient but suffer from limited, fixed-size storage. We introduce Fast-weight Product Key Memory (FwPKM), a sparse fast-weight memory layer that resolves this tension. FwPKM update…
items.sm: Introduces a sparse memory layer that updates selected parameters during training and inference to store and retrieve new associations with fixed per-token computation.

Building on a conditional VAE backbone, we replace the…
items.sm: Introduces FedHypeVAE, which uses a shared hypernetwork to generate personalized embedding generators while applying differential privacy to aggregated client gradients.

items.t: Controllable Concept Bottleneck Models

items.x: Machine unlearning offers a promising solution to privacy and safety concerns in large language models (LLMs) by selectively removing targeted knowledge while preserving utility. However, current methods are highly sensitive to downstream fine-tuning, which can quickly recover forgotten information-even from unrelated tasks. To address this, we introduce invariance into unlearning for the first time, inspired by inva…
items.sm: Proposes invariance-based regularization to keep removed language model knowledge from returning during downstream fine-tuning, including on previously unseen tasks.

items.x: Large language models (LLMs) encode vast world knowledge but struggle to stay up-to-date, often leading to errors and hallucinations. Knowledge editing offers an efficient alternative to retraining, enabling targeted modifications by updating specific model parameters. However, existing methods primarily focus on individual models, posing challenges in efficiently updating multiple models and adapting to new models. …

items.sm: Introduces WARP, a recurrent model that represents its hidden state as auxiliary network parameters, enabling gradient-free adaptation during inference.

items.x: Knowledge editing aims to efficiently update Large Language Models (LLMs) by modifying specific knowledge without retraining the entire model.Among knowledge editing approaches, in-context editing (ICE) offers a lightweight solution by injecting new knowledge directly into the input context, leaving model parameters unchanged.However, existing ICE approaches do not explicitly separate the newly injected knowledge fro…

items.t: MEMOIR: Lifelong Model Editing with Minimal Overwrite and Informed Retention for LLMs
items.a: Ke Wang, Yiming Qin, Nikolaos Dimitriadis, Alessandro Favero, Pascal Frossard
items.x: Language models deployed in real-world systems often require post-hoc updates to incorporate new or corrected knowledge. However, editing such models efficiently and reliably-without retraining or forgetting previous information-remains a major challenge. Existing methods for lifelong model editing either compromise generalization, interfere with past edits, or fail to scale to long editing sequences. We propose MEMO…
items.sm: Introduces MEMOIR, which stores knowledge edits in a separate residual memory and uses sparse activation patterns to limit interference and retrieve relevant edits.

items.t: COMPKE: Complex Question Answering under Knowledge Editing

items.x: Knowledge Editing-Efficiently modifying the knowledge in large language models has gathered great attention.Current benchmarks primarily use multi-hop question answering to assess and analyze newly injected or updated knowledge.However, we argue that these benchmarks fail to effectively evaluate how well the updated models apply this knowledge in real-life scenarios, particularly when questions require complex reason…
items.sm: Introduces COMPKE, a benchmark of 11,924 complex questions testing whether edited language models apply updated knowledge through relational and logical reasoning.

items.sm: Introduces MedEditBench to evaluate medical knowledge editing and proposes editing model-generated rationales to address poor generalization from simple factual updates.

items.t: External Data-Enhanced Meta-Representation for Adaptive Probabilistic Load Forecasting
items.a: Haoran Li, Muhao Guo, Marija Ilić, Yang Weng, Guangchun Ruan

items.sm: Uses hypernetworks to adapt electricity load forecasting parameters to external conditions, with selectively activated experts supporting efficiency and robustness.

items.sm: Introduces a parameter generator that converts a few unlabeled task prompts into LoRA updates, avoiding separate training for each downstream task.

items.a: Kazuki Irie, Morris Yau, Samuel Joseph Gershman
items.x: We develop hybrid memory architectures for general-purpose sequence processing neural networks, that combine key-value memory using softmax attention (KV-memory) with fast weight memory through dynamic synaptic modulation (FW-memory) -- the core principles of quadratic and linear transformers, respectively. These two memory systems have complementary but individually limited properties: KV-memory offers precise retri…
items.sm: Compares three hybrid architectures combining softmax attention memory with fast weight memory to balance precise retrieval and efficient processing of long sequences.

Existing TTT methods struggled to show effectiveness in handling long-context data, due to their inefficiency on modern GPUs. The TTT layers in many of these app…
items.sm: Proposes updating fast weights using much larger chunks during test-time training to address poor GPU utilization and restrictive causal dependencies.

This raises the question: is it possible to transfer fine-tuning to a new release of the model? In this work, we inves…

items.a: Youssef, Paul, Zhixue Zhao, Christin Seifert, Jörg Schlötterer

In order to defend against these types of malicious manipulation, we need robust techniques that can reliably detect, interpret…

items.x: While large language models (LLMs) have enabled learning knowledge from the pre-training corpora, the acquired knowledge may be fundamentally incorrect or outdated over time, which necessitates rectifying the knowledge of the language model (LM) after the training. A promising approach involves employing a hyper-network to generate parameter shift, whereas existing hyper-networks suffer from inferior scalability in s…
items.sm: Introduces MALMEN, which combines hypernetwork-generated parameter updates through least squares to support simultaneous editing of many language model facts within memory limits.

items.t: Task Arithmetic with LoRA for Continual Learning
items.a: Rajas Chitale, Ankit Vaidya, Aditya Kane, Archana Santosh Ghotkar
items.x: Continual learning refers to the problem where the training data is available in sequential chunks, termed "tasks". The majority of progress in continual learning has been stunted by the problem of catastrophic forgetting, which is caused by sequential training of the model on streams of data. Moreover, it becomes computationally expensive to sequentially train large models multiple times. To mitigate both of these p…
items.sm: Combines low-rank adaptation and task arithmetic for continual learning in vision transformers, claiming to avoid catastrophic forgetting while reducing training costs.

items.t: LM-Cocktail: Resilient Tuning of Language Models via Model Merging
items.a: Shitao Xiao, Zheng Liu, Peitian Zhang, Xingrun Xing
items.v: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL (Findings of ACL)
items.x: The pre-trained language models are continually fine-tuned to better support downstream applications.However, this operation may result in significant performance degeneration on general tasks beyond the targeted domain.To overcome this problem, we propose LM-Cocktail which enables the fine-tuned model to stay resilient in general perspectives.Our method is conducted in the form of model merging, where the fine-tuned…
items.sm: Introduces LM-Cocktail, which averages fine-tuned language models with base or other domain models to preserve general capabilities while retaining domain performance.

items.t: Language and Task Arithmetic with Parameter-Efficient Layers for Zero-Shot Summarization
items.a: Alexandra Chronopoulou, Jonas Pfeiffer, Joshua Maynez, Xinyi Wang, Sebastian Ruder, Priyanka Agrawal
items.x: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) using labeled task data can significantly improve the performance of large language models (LLMs) on the downstream task.However, there are 7000 languages in the world and many of these languages lack labeled data for real-world language generation tasks.In this paper, we propose to improve zero-shot cross-lingual transfer by composing expert modules trained separately on langua…
items.sm: Combines separately trained language and task adapters through arithmetic operations to improve zero-shot cross-lingual summarization using unlabeled language data and labeled task data.

items.t: DUnE: Dataset for Unified Editing
items.a: Afra Feyza Akyürek, Eric Pan, Garry Kuwanto, Derry Tanti Wijaya
items.v: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
items.x: Even the most advanced language models remain susceptible to errors necessitating to modify these models without initiating a comprehensive retraining process.Model editing refers to the modification of a model's knowledge or representations in a manner that produces the desired outcomes.Prior research primarily centered around editing factual data e.g."Messi plays for Inter Miami" confining the definition of an edit…
items.sm: Introduces DUnE, a benchmark that broadens language model editing beyond factual changes to natural language requests addressing biases, reasoning errors, and other outputs.

items.t: Scalable and Efficient Continual Learning from Demonstration via a Hypernetwork-generated Stable Dynamics Model
items.a: Sayantan Auddy, Jakob Hollenstein, Matteo Saveriano, Antonio J. Rodríguez-Sánchez, Justus Piater
items.v: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive and Developmental Systems
items.x: Robots capable of learning from demonstration (LfD) must exhibit stability while executing learned motion skills. To be effective in the real world, they should also remember multiple skills over time – a capability lacking in current stable-LfD methods. We propose an approach to stable, continual LfD, and highlight the role of stability in improving continual learning. Our proposed hypernetwork generates the paramet…
items.sm: Uses a hypernetwork to generate stable robot motion models, enabling continual learning from demonstrations while reducing cumulative training time from quadratic to linear.

items.t: Finding and Editing Multi-Modal Neurons in Pre-Trained Transformers
items.a: Haowen Pan, Yixin Cao, Xiaozhi Wang, Xun Yang, Meng Wang
items.v: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL (Findings of ACL)
items.x: Understanding the internal mechanisms by which multi-modal large language models (LLMs) interpret different modalities and integrate cross-modal representations is becoming increasingly critical for continuous improvements in both academia and industry. In this paper, we propose a novel method to identify key neurons for interpretability -- how multi-modal LLMs bridge visual and textual concepts for captioning. Our m…
items.sm: Identifies neurons linking visual and textual concepts without gradient calculations, then edits them to reduce sensitive language or hallucinations in multimodal models.

items.t: A Generalized Physical-knowledge-guided Dynamic Model for Underwater Image Enhancement
items.a: Pan Mu, Hanning Xu, Zheyuan Liu, Zheng Wang, Sixian Chan, Cong Bai
items.v: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
items.x: Underwater images often suffer from color distortion and low contrast resulting in various image types, due to the scattering and absorption of light by water. While it is difficult to obtain high-quality paired training samples with a generalized model. To tackle these challenges, we design a Generalized Underwater image enhancement method via a Physical-knowledge-guided Dynamic Model (short for GUPDM). In particula…
items.sm: Combines physical simulations of underwater lighting with adaptive network components to enhance images affected by color distortion and low contrast.

items.t: HyperFields: Towards Zero-Shot Generation of NeRFs from Text
items.a: Sudarshan Babu, Liu, Richard, Zhou, Avery, Michael Maire, Gregory Shakhnarovich, Rana Hanocka
items.x: We introduce HyperFields, a method for generating text-conditioned Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) with a single forward pass and (optionally) some fine-tuning. Key to our approach are: (i) a dynamic hypernetwork, which learns a smooth mapping from text token embeddings to the space of NeRFs; (ii) NeRF distillation training, which distills scenes encoded in individual NeRFs into one dynamic hypernetwork. These techniq…
items.sm: HyperFields uses a hypernetwork trained on existing scenes to generate neural radiance fields from text, directly or with limited fine-tuning.

items.t: From Pointwise to Powerhouse: Initialising Neural Networks with Generative Models
items.a: Christian Harder, Moritz Fuchs, Yuri Tolkach, Anirban Mukhopadhyay
items.x: Traditional initialisation methods, e.g. He and Xavier, have been effective in avoiding the problem of vanishing or exploding gradients in neural networks. However, they only use simple pointwise distributions, which model one-dimensional variables. Moreover, they ignore most information about the architecture and disregard past training experiences. These limitations can be overcome by employing generative models fo…
items.sm: Uses variational autoencoders and graph hypernetworks to initialize neural network weights, evaluating their effects on accuracy, convergence speed, and ensembles.

items.t: HAMUR: Hyper Adapter for Multi-Domain Recommendation
items.a: Xiaopeng Li, Yan Bin Fan, Xiangyu Zhao, Yichao Wang, Bo Chen, Huifeng Guo, Ruiming Tang
items.v: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
items.x: Multi-Domain Recommendation (MDR) has gained significant attention in recent years, which leverages data from multiple domains to enhance their performance concurrently. However, current MDR models are confronted with two limitations. Firstly, the majority of these models adopt an approach that explicitly shares parameters between domains, leading to mutual interference among them. Secondly, due to the distribution d…
items.sm: HAMUR combines domain-specific adapters with a shared hypernetwork to adapt recommendations across domains while reducing interference from shared parameters.

items.t: Deep Task-specific Bottom Representation Network for Multi-Task Recommendation
items.a: Qi Liu, Zhilong Zhou, Gangwei Jiang, Tiezheng Ge, Defu Lian
items.v: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
items.x: Neural-based multi-task learning (MTL) has gained significant improvement, and it has been successfully applied to recommendation system (RS). Recent deep MTL methods for RS (e.g. MMoE, PLE) focus on designing soft gating-based parameter-sharing networks that implicitly learn a generalized representation for each task. However, MTL methods may suffer from performance degeneration when dealing with conflicting tasks, …
items.sm: Introduces task-specific input representations for multitask recommendation to reduce interference between conflicting tasks and better capture each task's characteristics.

items.t: HyperBandit: Contextual Bandit with Hypernewtork for Time-Varying User Preferences in Streaming Recommendation
items.a: Chenglei Shen, Xiao Zhang, Wei Wei, Jun Xu
items.v: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
items.x: In real-world streaming recommender systems, user preferences often dynamically change over time (e.g., a user may have different preferences during weekdays and weekends). Existing bandit-based streaming recommendation models only consider time as a timestamp, without explicitly modeling the relationship between time variables and time-varying user preferences. This leads to recommendation models that cannot quickly…
items.sm: HyperBandit uses time features and a hypernetwork to adjust a contextual bandit's reward predictions as user preferences change.

items.sm: Introduces an algorithm providing user-level differential privacy for hypernetwork-based personalized federated learning, reporting stronger privacy protection with modest utility losses.

items.t: Localizing and Editing Knowledge in Text-to-Image Generative Models
items.a: Samyadeep Basu, Nanxuan Zhao, Vlad I. Morariu, Soheil Feizi, Varun Manjunatha
items.x: Text-to-Image Diffusion Models such as Stable-Diffusion and Imagen have achieved unprecedented quality of photorealism with state-of-the-art FID scores on MS-COCO and other generation benchmarks. Given a caption, image generation requires fine-grained knowledge about attributes such as object structure, style, and viewpoint amongst others. Where does this information reside in text-to-image generative models? In our …
items.sm: Uses causal mediation analysis to locate knowledge about visual attributes within the image generation network and text encoder of text-to-image diffusion models.

items.t: Equivariant Deep Weight Space Alignment
items.a: Aviv Navon, Aviv Shamsian, Ethan Fetaya, Gal Chechik, Nadav Dym, Haggai Maron
items.x: Permutation symmetries of deep networks make basic operations like model merging and similarity estimation challenging. In many cases, aligning the weights of the networks, i.e., finding optimal permutations between their weights, is necessary. Unfortunately, weight alignment is an NP-hard problem. Prior research has mainly focused on solving relaxed versions of the alignment problem, leading to either time-consuming…
items.sm: Deep-Align learns to align neural network weights without labeled examples using an architecture that respects the alignment problem's symmetries.

items.t: Learning to (Learn at Test Time)
items.a: Yu Sun, Li, Xinhao, Karan Dalal, Chloe Hsu, Sanmi Koyejo, Carlos Guestrin, Xiaolong Wang, Tatsunori Hashimoto
items.x: We reformulate the problem of supervised learning as learning to learn with two nested loops (i.e. learning problems). The inner loop learns on each individual instance with self-supervision before final prediction. The outer loop learns the self-supervised task used by the inner loop, such that its final prediction improves. Our inner loop turns out to be equivalent to linear attention when the inner-loop learner is…
items.sm: Trains models to learn from each input through self-supervision before prediction, while an outer training loop learns which self-supervised task improves predictions.

items.t: Model Merging by Uncertainty-Based Gradient Matching
items.a: Nico Daheim, Thomas Möllenhoff, Edoardo Maria Ponti, Iryna Gurevych, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan
items.x: Models trained on different datasets can be merged by a weighted-averaging of their parameters, but why does it work and when can it fail? Here, we connect the inaccuracy of weighted-averaging to mismatches in the gradients and propose a new uncertainty-based scheme to improve the performance by reducing the mismatch. The connection also reveals implicit assumptions in other schemes such as averaging, task arithmetic…
items.sm: Connects model merging errors to gradient mismatches and introduces uncertainty-based weighting that improves merged language models and vision transformers.

items.t: Evaluating the Reversal Curse in Model Editing
items.a: Xu, Hao-Xiang, Jun-Yu Ma, Zhen-Hua Ling, Quan Liu, Cong Liu, Gu, Jia-Chen
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) are prone to hallucinate unintended text due to false or outdated knowledge. Since retraining LLMs is resource intensive, there has been a growing interest in model editing. Despite the emergence of benchmarks and approaches, existing unidirectional editing and evaluation paradigms have failed to explore the reversal curse. In this paper, we study bidirectional language model editing, aim…
items.sm: Introduces a benchmark and metric testing whether edited language models can recall updated facts when queried in the reverse direction.

items.t: A Symmetry-Aware Exploration of Bayesian Neural Network Posteriors
items.a: Laurent, Olivier, Emanuel Aldea, Gianni Franchi

This paper proposes one of the first large-scale explorations of the posterior distribution of deep Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs), expanding its study to real-world vision tasks and architectures. Specifically, we inv…
items.sm: Examines Bayesian neural network weight distributions on vision tasks, focusing on approximation quality, uncertainty estimates, and the effects of permutation and scaling symmetries.

items.t: HyperTab: Hypernetwork Approach for Deep Learning on Small Tabular Datasets
items.a: Witold Wydmański, Oleksii Bulenok, Marek Śmieja
items.v: IEEE International Conference on Data Science and Advanced Analytics (DSAA)
items.x: Deep learning has achieved impressive performance in many domains, such as computer vision and natural language processing, but its advantage over classical shallow methods on tabular datasets remains questionable. It is especially challenging to surpass the performance of tree-like ensembles, such as XGBoost or Random Forests, on small-sized datasets (less than 1k samples). To tackle this challenge, we introduce Hyp…
items.sm: HyperTab uses a hypernetwork to generate neural network ensembles specialized for different feature subsets, addressing learning from small tabular datasets.

Model fusion methods, such as task arithmetic, have been proven to be powerful and scalable to incorporate fine-tuned weights from different tasks into a multi-task model. However, efficiently fine-tuning large pre-trained models on multiple downstream tasks remains challenging, leading to inefficient m…

items.t: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
items.a: Omar Khattab, Arnav Singhvi, Paridhi Maheshwari, Zhiyuan Zhang, Keshav Santhanam, Sri Vardhamanan, Saiful Haq, Sharma, Ashutosh
items.x: The ML community is rapidly exploring techniques for prompting language models (LMs) and for stacking them into pipelines that solve complex tasks. Unfortunately, existing LM pipelines are typically implemented using hard-coded "prompt templates", i.e. lengthy strings discovered via trial and error. Toward a more systematic approach for developing and optimizing LM pipelines, we introduce DSPy, a programming model th…
items.sm: Introduces DSPy, a programming model and compiler that optimize modular language model pipelines against a chosen metric instead of relying on manually written prompts.

items.t: AdaMerging: Adaptive Model Merging for Multi-Task Learning
items.a: Enneng Yang, Zhenyi Wang, Shen, Li, Shiwei Liu, Guibing Guo, Xingwei Wang, Dacheng Tao
items.x: Multi-task learning (MTL) aims to empower a model to tackle multiple tasks simultaneously. A recent development known as task arithmetic has revealed that several models, each fine-tuned for distinct tasks, can be directly merged into a single model to execute MTL without necessitating a retraining process using the initial training data. Nevertheless, this direct addition of models often leads to a significant deter…
items.sm: AdaMerging learns coefficients for combining task-specific models into a multitask model without using their original training data.

items.t: Unveiling the Pitfalls of Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models
items.a: Zhoubo Li, Ningyu Zhang, Yunzhi Yao, Mengru Wang, Xi Chen, Huajun Chen
items.x: As the cost associated with fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) continues to rise, recent research efforts have pivoted towards developing methodologies to edit implicit knowledge embedded within LLMs. Yet, there's still a dark cloud lingering overhead -- will knowledge editing trigger butterfly effect? since it is still unclear whether knowledge editing might introduce side effects that pose potential risks or …
items.sm: Introduces benchmarks and metrics for knowledge editing risks, examining how edits can amplify conflicting facts or distort a language model's knowledge.

items.t: Merge, Then Compress: Demystify Efficient SMoE with Hints from Its Routing Policy
items.a: Pingzhi Li, Zhenyu Zhang, Prateek Yadav, Yi-Lin Sung, Yu Cheng, Mohit Bansal, Tianlong Chen

Therefore, vanilla SMoE models are memory inefficient and non-s…
items.sm: Investigates merging and compressing experts in sparsely activated mixture-of-experts models, using routing behavior to address redundant information and high memory use.

items.t: A Re-Parameterized Vision Transformer (ReVT) for Domain-Generalized Semantic Segmentation
items.a: Jan-Aike Termöhlen, Timo Bartels, Tim Fingscheidt

However, the performance of such models degrades when deployed in an unseen domain with different data distributions compared to the training domain. We present a new augmentation-driven approach to domain generalization for semantic segmentation using a re-parameterized vision transformer (ReVT) with weight averag…
items.sm: Combines data augmentation with averaging trained vision transformer weights to improve semantic segmentation on unseen domains without adding inference computation.

items.t: CoroNetGAN: Controlled Pruning of GANs via Hypernetworks

However, the unprecedented demand for the deployment of GANs on resource-constrained edge devices still poses a challenge due to huge number of parameters involved in the generation process. This has led to focused attention on the area of compressing GANs. Most…
items.sm: CoroNetGAN uses hypernetworks and differentiable pruning to compress generative adversarial networks during training while allowing control over the compression level.

items.t: HyperCoil-Recon: A Hypernetwork-based Adaptive Coil Configuration Task Switching Network for MRI Reconstruction
items.a: Sriprabha Ramanarayanan, Mohammad Al Fahim, G. S. Rahul, Amrit Kumar Jethi, Keerthi Ram, Mohanasankar Sivaprakasam
items.v: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops

items.sm: HyperCoil-Recon uses hypernetworks to generate configuration-specific weights for MRI reconstruction across varying numbers of receiver coils.

items.t: Neural Processing of Tri-Plane Hybrid Neural Fields

Early approaches employ neural fields parameterized by shared networks trained on the whole dataset, achieving good task performance but sacrificing reconstruction quality.…
items.sm: Investigates directly processing tri-plane hybrid neural fields for tasks involving three-dimensional data, including classification and part segmentation.

items.t: Editing Implicit Assumptions in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
items.a: Hadas Orgad, Bahjat Kawar, Yonatan Belinkov

While some assumptions are useful (e.g., the sky is blue), they can also be outdated, incorrect, or reflective of social biases present in the training data. Thus, there is a need to control these assumptions without requiring explicit user input or costly re-training. In this work, we aim to edit a given implicit a…

However, the lack of a regular and explicit grid structure also makes it challenging to apply generative modeling directly on implicit neural fields in order to synthesize new data. To this en…

items.t: Masked Hard-Attention Transformers Recognize Exactly the Star-Free Languages

items.t: Emptying the Ocean with a Spoon: Should We Edit Models?

As a result, these datasets contain few labeled images, and current machine vision models cannot train inte…
